platform_features.title: HTTPS and local CA
platform_features.summary: Optional HTTPS gateway with a persisted ECDSA P-256 local CA, a leaf per requested AWS, LocalStack or localhost name, extra DNS/IP names, supplied certificate/key support, and CA PEM export. Trust, DNS and port forwarding remain manual.

platform_features.title: Fault injection
platform_features.summary: Ordered gateway rules inject protocol-correct AWS errors and cancellable latency by service, operation, Region and account, with probability, startup configuration, reset restoration, diagnostics and LocalStack Chaos API aliases.

platform_features.title: AWS wire protocols
platform_features.summary: AWS JSON 1.0/1.1, AWS Query, EC2 Query, REST XML/JSON, and Smithy RPC v2 CBOR through generated bindings.

platform_features.title: Identity and resource scope
platform_features.summary: Configured access-key accounts, 12-digit access keys that are their own account ID, IAM/STS credential lookup, regional and account-wide scopes, optional SigV4 verification, and identity-policy evaluation with off, soft and enforce modes.

platform_features.title: Transactional storage and persistence
platform_features.summary: Atomic callback transactions, in-memory storage, and optional SQLite commit persistence with resource reload on restart; runtime and in-flight state have separate limits.

platform_features.title: Cloudscape console
platform_features.summary: AWS-style dark dashboard with configurable widgets, a favorites bar of starred services, visit history, categorized service catalog with AWS icons, shared top-bar account/Region menus with configured-account choices, resource inventory/details, IAM, S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch metrics/alarms/dashboard, API Gateway HTTP/REST, Step Functions, EC2/VPC management workflows, and account-wide Budgets with actual spend, Cost Explorer charts and fixture management, and CUR report management, in-memory signed root console sessions for verify mode, IAM authorization status and explained request decisions, recent requests, delivery history, and metrics through a separately served web console.

platform_features.title: Diagnostics
platform_features.summary: Health/resource endpoints, bounded request and delivery logs, outbound message inspection (email, SMS, Cognito codes) with LocalStack-compatible SES and SNS aliases, model-sensitive body redaction, and Prometheus request metrics.

platform_features.title: Init hooks and reset
platform_features.summary: LocalStack-style boot, start, ready and shutdown scripts (also read from /etc/localstack/init) with a status endpoint, idempotent IAM/S3/SQS sample data in the development example config, and a POST reset endpoint that clears all stored state and can re-run the ready scripts.

platform_features.title: CLI and SDK clients
platform_features.summary: Local endpoint overrides for AWS clients, CLI wrappers (aws, terraform, sam, cdk), and generated Go SDK-compatible APIs.

platform_features.title: Infrastructure workflows
platform_features.summary: Selected Terraform AWS provider workflows, AWS SAM and CDK (bootstrap and deploy) through the registered CloudFormation resource-type subset.

platform_features.title: Runtime adapters
platform_features.summary: Docker Lambda execution and opt-in ECS Docker tasks, EKS k3s clusters, and ElastiCache Docker nodes; default optional adapters manage records.

platform_features.title: Cross-service event delivery
platform_features.summary: Supported notification, rule, and event-source workflows connect local service implementations and record delivery outcomes.

platform_features.title: Console single sign-on
platform_features.summary: Optional OpenID Connect sign-in to the console (authorization code with PKCE, any compliant provider such as Authelia, Zitadel, Keycloak, Authentik, Okta or Entra ID). Provider groups grant all matching IAM roles, deduplicated in configuration order; people with several roles choose an account and role in an access portal and can switch within their server-owned allowed set from the Account menu. Only the active role grants administrative access. The person gets the selected role's temporary STS credentials, so IAM authorization and the request inspector apply per person, and the administrative endpoints require an administrator's session or root credentials. `tinystack login` signs the AWS CLI in the same way through the device authorization flow, with HTTPS outside loopback, single-use fresh tokens and private atomic credential caches and an explicit --role selection for multi-role users. Enforced member inventory omits details and evaluates request conditions; mapped role deletion invalidates old federated credentials.

platform_features.title: Console CloudShell
platform_features.summary: A browser terminal in console builds that executes the real host AWS CLI with streamed output, quotes and escapes, a scrubbed environment and a forced TinyStack API endpoint. Local mode uses the selected account; verify mode issues short-lived STS credentials for the verified console principal so normal gateway IAM applies. Every CLI command runs with aws_completer completion unless console.cloudshell.allow lists service:command patterns such as s3:*, which then limit both commands and completion; with OIDC/SSO CloudShell is administrator-only. Command bodies and output are redacted in the inspector, requests are capped at 64 KiB, and at most four commands run concurrently. AWS CLI v2 must be installed separately; the Docker image does not include it. No shell features or interactive prompts; history stays in memory. The opening banner identifies the console principal and account. Silent successful commands print a dim (no output) line.

platform_features.title: Optional DNS listener
platform_features.summary: Opt-in UDP/TCP split DNS for AWS endpoint and resource names, default-account Route 53 records, and upstream forwarding. HTTP gateway; default HTTPS clients need a trusted TLS reverse proxy and port mapping.

platform_features.title: Instance and container metadata
platform_features.summary: EC2 IMDSv1/v2 under /_tinystack/imds and an optional dedicated /latest listener, with explicit instance selection and STS instance-profile credentials. Verify mode requires the dedicated listener for IMDS credentials. Docker ECS tasks receive host-reachable metadata v4 and task-role credential endpoints; tokens are removed when tasks stop.

mediaconvert.title: AWS Elemental MediaConvert
mediaconvert.summary: Manage queues, custom presets and job templates and exercise a durable local job lifecycle without transcoding.
features: Queue, preset and job-template CRUD, tags, category and partial-input filters and indexed name/creation-date pagination with ascending/descending order
Per-account/Region Default queue; ON_DEMAND pricing, pause/resume, priority/concurrency scheduling and active-job deletion checks
Create/Get/List/Search/Cancel jobs with existing local IAM roles, queues, templates and preset references; one-minute client-token idempotency
Template defaults merge recursively with explicit job settings; supplied arrays replace template arrays
Persisted SUBMITTED → PROGRESSING → COMPLETE execution, with timing, percent complete and empty queue transitions (queue hopping is unsupported)
Local S3 input existence validation; missing inputs finish ERROR with code 1404 and HeadObject failure message
MediaConvert Job State Change events publish to EventBridge after committed status changes, including CANCELED and ERROR; normal EventBridge rules deliver to local SQS targets
DescribeEndpoints returns the requesting TinyStack endpoint; inventory and Resource Groups Tagging integration
CloudFormation AWS::MediaConvert::Queue, Preset and JobTemplate; SettingsJson stores supported settings; Name changes replace and other supported properties update in place
Terraform aws_media_convert_queue (provider 5.100), endpoint override and in-place tag updates
gaps: No transcoding, probing or output media/manifest files: COMPLETE means local input objects existed, regardless of their bytes or codec
Only custom presets/templates are listed; no system preset/template catalog, reserved pricing, acceleration, queue hopping or inference feeds

Only profiled settings are accepted: S3 FileInput, basic input selectors, file output groups, MP4/container/video H264/audio AAC configuration, timecode and ad-avail offset; other model members fail explicitly
No HTTP input fetching, output object writes, codec validation, IAM data-plane permission simulation or periodic STATUS_UPDATE events; StatusUpdateInterval is stored
EventBridge publishing is best effort after commit; no transactional outbox/replay guarantee

datasync.title: AWS DataSync
datasync.summary: Store S3 and EFS locations and Basic tasks; execute persistent, queued local S3-to-S3 copies with filtering, deletion and verification.
features: Twenty JSON 1.1 operations at the pinned model; generated InvalidRequestException input constraint validation
S3 locations validate existing buckets and IAM roles, store storage class and prefixes, and expose AWS location ARNs and URIs
EFS location records validate file systems, access points, IAM roles, subnets and security groups; access points and roles require TLS1_2
Task create, describe, list, update and delete with stored options, includes, excludes, schedules and validated CloudWatch log group references
LocationUri, LocationType, CreationTime and task LocationId list filters, explicit unsupported operator errors and key-order pagination
Real S3-to-S3 task executions use an interruptible background queue, progress persisted after each batch of up to 100 objects, and one active execution per task
CHANGED compares size and ETag; ALL copies every selected object; NEVER skips existing destinations; REMOVE deletes selected destination objects absent at source
SIMPLE_PATTERN filters support pipe alternatives and wildcard matching, including AWS rightmost-only include wildcards; exclusions take precedence
Verification compares object contents, with NONE, ONLY_FILES_TRANSFERRED and POINT_IN_TIME_CONSISTENT modes and execution counters and phase results
Tags on locations, tasks and executions, Resource Groups Tagging API integration and resource inventory
CloudFormation AWS::DataSync::LocationS3, AWS::DataSync::LocationEFS and AWS::DataSync::Task with documented replacement properties
Terraform aws_datasync_location_s3 and aws_datasync_task lifecycle coverage and datasync endpoint override
gaps: Agents require real appliance activation; agents, NFS and SMB locations (required agent references), HDFS, FSx, object storage and Azure Blob locations are unsupported
Storage system discovery, Enhanced mode, manifests, task reports and UpdateTaskExecution are unsupported
EFS locations are records only; StartTaskExecution explicitly rejects any non-S3 location

Schedules, LogLevel and filesystem metadata options are stored only: no scheduled execution, CloudWatch log delivery or filesystem metadata application; bandwidth throttling is rejected except the unlimited -1 default

No distributed S3 snapshot: concurrent source changes can fail verification; cancellation or a process interruption may leave copies from the current batch of up to 100 objects applied before progress commits, and restart repeats that batch
No S3 access-point or Outposts locations, multipart copy, remote AWS access or IAM role assumption; S3 service local object size and storage behavior apply
Queue processing is FIFO per task using persisted sequence keys; progress counters model selected objects and bytes, with no network compression or measured phase durations
datasync.execution: Background local S3-to-S3 copies; EFS locations and schedules are records only

dynamodb.title: DynamoDB
dynamodb.summary: Store typed items and run expressions, transactions, streams, backups, exports, and PartiQL locally.
features: HASH and optional RANGE keys, global and local secondary indexes, sparse indexes and pagination
Nested condition, projection, filter, update and key expressions
Atomic batch and transaction operations with cancellation reasons and idempotency tokens
TTL sweeps, on-demand backups, latest-state point-in-time restores and S3 exports
PartiQL statements and transaction execution

Kinesis Data Streams streaming destinations (enable, update the timestamp precision, disable, describe; up to two active per table, one per stream): every committed item change, including batch, transaction, PartiQL and TTL writes, is put into the stream after the commit as a DynamoDB JSON record with both images, whether or not the table has a DynamoDB stream; AWS::DynamoDB::Table KinesisStreamSpecification

AWS-style console with scoped table creation/deletion, primary and secondary keys, index management, typed item creation/editing/deletion, explicit query/scan with filters and pagination, capacity settings, TTL, tags, streams and Lambda connections

AWS/DynamoDB metrics for PutItem, GetItem, DeleteItem, UpdateItem, Query, Scan, BatchGetItem, BatchWriteItem, TransactGetItems, TransactWriteItems and PartiQL (ExecuteStatement, BatchExecuteStatement, ExecuteTransaction): ConsumedReadCapacityUnits and ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits (item size over 4 KB or 1 KB, halved for eventually consistent reads and doubled for transactions) by TableName, TimeToLiveDeletedItemCount (Count) by TableName for TTL sweeps, SuccessfulRequestLatency (Milliseconds) and ThrottledRequests (always 0) by TableName and Operation, and UserErrors (4xx results, no dimensions) as in AWS
gaps: Index queries scan the table and are immediately consistent; no independent index storage
No throughput enforcement or capacity accounting; batch writes do not simulate throttling
Point-in-time restores retain the latest state, not historical snapshots
Legacy expression parameters and replica management are outside the subset

Kinesis destinations turn on at once (Enable reports ENABLING, Describe ACTIVE); records are put after the item write commits, so concurrent writes to one item can arrive out of order, and a destination whose stream was deleted becomes ENABLE_FAILED until it is enabled again; DescribeTable does not list destinations
Verify mode shows table inventory; item reads and management require signed CLI/SDK requests
Backups, restores, exports, PartiQL, batch and transaction operations use the AWS API rather than console forms
DynamoDB metrics leave out index dimensions (GlobalSecondaryIndexName), ReturnedItemCount, SystemErrors and ConditionalCheckFailedRequests; TinyStack never throttles, so ThrottledRequests stays 0

dynamodbstreams.title: DynamoDB Streams
dynamodbstreams.summary: Read the stream records written atomically with DynamoDB item changes.
features: List and describe streams, obtain shard iterators, and read records
Stream view types follow the table configuration
Lambda event source mappings consume stream records in-process
gaps: No shard splits or production-scale stream behavior
Only the fields selected in the profile are supported

s3.title: S3
s3.summary: Store object metadata in the shared store and object/version/multipart bytes in local files.
features: Partition-wide bucket name uniqueness and ownership checks
Object CRUD, listing, metadata, tagging, copy, upload checksum validation, one byte range and conditional requests
Multipart upload lifecycle and atomic completion, concatenating part files without buffering the complete object
Disk-backed objects and parts in both storage modes, streaming HTTP downloads including byte ranges, startup migration and orphan collection with transactional counts for shared file references
Streaming HTTP uploads for PutObject and UploadPart directly into disk-backed blob files with bounded memory, supporting ordinary, chunked and aws-chunked formats with trailing checksum validation
Stored object checksums (CRC32, CRC32C, CRC64NVME by default, SHA-1, SHA-256) returned with ChecksumMode, composite and full-object multipart checksums, kept through copies and versions
Versioning, null versions and delete markers
Presigned requests, bucket CORS and notifications to SQS, SNS, Lambda and EventBridge
Bucket lifecycle and encryption configuration are stored
AWS-style console for scoped bucket creation, empty/delete, folder and object browsing, uploads/downloads/copies, version deletion, object tags and bucket configuration
Bucket policies participate in gateway soft/enforce authorization, including cross-account bucket/object access and owning-root policy recovery

With authorization on, notification destinations (SQS, SNS, Lambda) need their resource policy to allow s3.amazonaws.com for the bucket (aws:SourceArn, aws:SourceAccount); enforce mode fails PutBucketNotificationConfiguration with InvalidArgument, unless SkipDestinationValidation is set, and denies later deliveries, while soft mode records the denied check

Object Lock at bucket creation or on a versioned bucket: GOVERNANCE and COMPLIANCE retention, legal hold and default bucket retention; deleting a locked version fails AccessDenied, COMPLIANCE retention cannot be shortened, and GOVERNANCE is bypassed with x-amz-bypass-governance-retention (s3:BypassGovernanceRetention when authorization is on)

Browser POST uploads (multipart/form-data to the bucket): ${filename} keys, policy expiration and eq/starts-with/content-length-range conditions, every field covered by the policy, SigV4 policy signatures in verify mode, success_action_status 200/201/204 and success_action_redirect; the upload is authorized and stored as PutObject
gaps: Lifecycle rules do not expire or transition objects

Encryption settings are metadata; objects are not encrypted as an AWS S3 data plane would encrypt them, and writes asking for aws:kms are accepted and stored like AES256 objects (aws:kms:dsse is rejected)
No website endpoint or general ACL evaluation; resource policies do not govern in-process reads

POST form fields other than key, Content-Type, x-amz-meta-*, Object Lock, success_action_* and signature fields (acl, tagging, storage class, encryption, cache headers) return NotImplemented; SigV2 POST signatures are unsupported
Generated in-process PutObject/UploadPart byte-slice shapes, in-process reads (e.g. Lambda runtime Object() helper), and console download and preview buffers still buffer bytes in memory

Verify-mode SigV4 authentication spools upload payloads to temporary files only when verifying signed hexadecimal or empty payload hashes; UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, supported unsigned-trailer forms (STREAMING-UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD-TRAILER), and usual presigned S3 uploads stream without that spool
Signed aws-chunked payloads (STREAMING-AWS4-HMAC-SHA256-*) remain unsupported and return NotImplemented

Console uploads are limited to 1 MiB per file; object browsing and management in verify mode require an authenticated root console session; storage.s3_max_object_bytes defaults to 256 MiB and can be set up to 5 GiB for object PUTs, parts and completed multipart objects

elasticache.title: ElastiCache
elasticache.summary: Manage Redis, Valkey, and Memcached resources with an optional Docker cache runtime.
features: Cache clusters, replication groups, serverless caches, subnet groups and parameter groups
Single-shard replication groups with replica scaling, primary/reader endpoints, manual and test failover, and AUTH token updates
Engine metadata, tags and lifecycle events
Docker nodes expose allocated host ports and become available after readiness probes
Records mode returns metadata without starting cache processes
gaps: Cache data is lost when containers are removed on shutdown or restart; persistent mode retains metadata only
Host ports can change when nodes restart
Production networking, topology and failover behavior are not reproduced
Multi-shard cluster mode, snapshots/backups and RBAC users/user groups are outside the subset
Reset removes the cache containers it started; a node starting during the reset can outlive it until shutdown

glue.title: Glue Data Catalog
glue.summary: Create the databases, tables, and partitions that local Athena queries use.
features: Database CRUD, tags and pagination
Table CRUD and batch deletion
Partition CRUD, batch operations and partition listings
Names are normalized to lowercase; deleting a database removes its tables and partitions
gaps: Only Data Catalog operations are implemented
ETL jobs, crawlers, workflows and production engines are not implemented

athena.title: Athena
athena.summary: Query local S3 data through the Glue catalog using an in-memory SQLite SQL engine.
features: Workgroups, named queries, query execution metadata, pagination and client tokens
SELECT queries over CSV, delimited text, JSON and Parquet, including gzip text and SNAPPY/GZIP/ZSTD Parquet pages
Glue catalog DDL, SHOW, DESCRIBE, MSCK REPAIR and partition changes
CTAS to Parquet, JSON or TEXTFILE, WITH NO DATA, and INSERT INTO SELECT or VALUES
Partitioned writes create Hive prefixes and Glue partitions; row update counts are retained
Query results are retained and written to the configured S3 output location
gaps: Queries complete inside StartQueryExecution; there is no distributed query engine
SQL is a documented SQLite-backed subset, not full Trino semantics
ORC, Avro, Iceberg and Iceberg-only mutation statements are rejected; bucketed CTAS properties are unsupported
athena.execution: SQLite SQL engine with local S3 reads/writes and Glue catalog updates

sqs.title: SQS
sqs.summary: Use queues with visibility timeouts, long polling, FIFO ordering, and dead-letter workflows.
features: Queue lifecycle, attributes and tags
Send, receive, delete, visibility updates and batch operations
Long polling waits outside transactions
FIFO deduplication and group ordering
Dead-letter queues and message move tasks

AWS-style console with account/Region-scoped standard and FIFO queue creation and editing, message send/receive/details/delete/visibility controls, typed purge/delete confirmations, tags, access and redrive allow policies, and standard-queue DLQ redrive task management
PurgeQueue clears available, delayed and in-flight messages while preserving settings and enforcing a 60-second repeat-purge guard
Queue Policy attributes and AddPermission grants participate in gateway soft/enforce authorization, including cross-account SendMessage and owning-root queue-policy recovery

With authorization on, SNS, S3 notification and EventBridge deliveries (including target dead-letter queues) need the queue policy to allow the service principal, matching aws:SourceArn and aws:SourceAccount; enforce mode drops a denied delivery and soft mode records it in the request inspector

AWS/SQS metrics with dimension QueueName: NumberOfMessagesSent and SentMessageSize (Bytes) for SendMessage, batches, SNS and EventBridge deliveries, NumberOfMessagesReceived, NumberOfEmptyReceives and NumberOfMessagesDeleted, and, sampled once a minute while the queue is in use, ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible, ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible, ApproximateNumberOfMessagesDelayed and ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage (Seconds)
gaps: No throughput enforcement
No message groups on standard queues or FIFO message move tasks
DeleteQueue does not enforce the AWS name-reuse delay
Purge completes immediately instead of an asynchronous deletion window; FIFO deduplication history is retained
In verify mode, console management requires an authenticated root console session; without a session only queue inventory is available

SQS metrics omit ApproximateNumberOfGroupsWithInflightMessages and the other FIFO metrics; a queue reports its approximate gauges only after a request since the process started and stops after six hours without requests, and a FIFO duplicate still counts as sent

sns.title: SNS
sns.summary: Publish messages to local queues and functions, or confirmed HTTP subscriptions.
features: Topics, tags, subscriptions, filtering and FIFO deduplication
SQS fan-out and asynchronous Lambda invocation
HTTP/HTTPS confirmation and outbound delivery
Email and SMS deliveries are recorded for inspection

AWS-style console with account/Region-scoped standard and FIFO topic creation, display names, deduplication, policies and tags; subscription lists and details, endpoint selection, confirmation and deletion, raw delivery and attribute/body filters; message publishing and topic-specific delivery inspection
Topic attributes report confirmed and pending subscription counts separately; inventory exposes pending status and filter configuration without confirmation tokens

Default topic policies and validated CreateTopic/SetTopicAttributes policies enforced in soft/enforce mode: same-account identity or resource Allow, cross-account both, explicit Deny precedence and owning-root Get/SetTopicAttributes recovery

With authorization on, S3 notification and EventBridge publications need the topic policy to allow s3.amazonaws.com or events.amazonaws.com, and deliveries to SQS queues and Lambda functions need their policies to allow sns.amazonaws.com with the topic as aws:SourceArn; a denied delivery fails like a missing queue and Publish still succeeds

AWS/SNS metrics with dimension TopicName: NumberOfMessagesPublished, NumberOfNotificationsDelivered and NumberOfNotificationsFailed, counted once per message and subscriber for SQS, Lambda, HTTP(S), email and SMS subscriptions
gaps: Email and SMS are recorded, not sent to providers
No mobile application or Firehose subscriptions, delivery retries or message signatures
SQS/Lambda subscription endpoints must belong to the subscriber's account
In verify mode, console management requires an authenticated root console session; without a session topic/subscription inventory and delivery history remain available
SNS metrics omit PublishSize, SMS metrics, filter policy and redrive metrics, and delivery metrics by protocol or application; confirmation messages are not counted

eventbridge.title: EventBridge
eventbridge.summary: Route events through local buses, patterns, rules, schedules, archives, and replays.
features: Default and custom buses, rules, targets and input transformers
Pattern matching shared with other event services
SQS, SNS and Lambda targets in the same account and region

Connections (API key, Basic and OAuth client credentials, with invocation header, query string and body parameters) and API destinations; Describe never returns secrets, and DeauthorizeConnection removes the credentials as AWS does

API destination targets make a real HTTP request with the rendered event as the body: the target's HttpParameters fill the endpoint's * wildcards and add headers and query string parameters, the connection adds its parameters (which win) and its authorization, OAuth access tokens are cached until they expire, and a response other than 2xx fails the delivery into the retry and dead-letter path (5xx, 401, 407, 409 and 429 are retried, other statuses go to the dead-letter queue at once)
Scheduled rules, durable retry records and SQS dead-letter queues
Archives and synchronous replay

AWS-style console for scoped event buses, rule patterns and schedules, nondelivering pattern tests, Lambda/SQS/SNS target selection and input/retry options, tags, explicit test-event publication and rule/bus delivery inspection
Gateway bus and rule resource-policy enforcement, explicit Deny precedence, and same-region cross-account bus ARN publication and rule management

With authorization on, SQS, SNS and Lambda targets without a role, and dead-letter queues, need their resource policy to allow events.amazonaws.com with the rule as aws:SourceArn; enforce mode fails the invocation into the existing retry and dead-letter path with the ERROR_CODE NO_PERMISSIONS, soft mode records the denied check

Targets with a RoleArn assume that role, whose trust policy must allow events.amazonaws.com for the rule (aws:SourceArn) and account, and are then decided by the role's policies and the target's resource policy; a role that cannot be assumed reports FAILED_TO_ASSUME_ROLE
gaps: No partner buses, cross-region bus references, event-bus targets or additional target service families
Connections always report AUTHORIZED or DEAUTHORIZED, and private connectivity and KMS keys are rejected

API destination deliveries are synchronous (PutEvents waits up to 5 seconds for each endpoint), are not authorized against the target's RoleArn, and send the event as the body for every method; HttpParameters values that are JSONPath references such as $.detail.id are rejected, and the OAuth token request is a form POST (or GET with query parameters) with Basic client authentication
Organization conditions and unsupported IAM policy elements are rejected; archive/replay management does not evaluate bus policies
Replays run synchronously and cannot be cancelled
Cron does not support L, W or #
Verify mode exposes bus/rule/target inventory and deliveries; management and event publication require signed CLI/SDK requests
Bus permissions, archives and replay management use the AWS API rather than console forms
With IAM authorization, conditions on events:source and events:detail-type fail closed for PutRule patterns with operators in those fields or a top-level $or
eventbridge.guide: With identity.authorization set to soft or enforce, bus and rule actions evaluate the owning bus policy. Cross-account calls use full bus or tagging ARNs and require identity plus resource Allow. PutEvents checks every entry before delivery; one denied entry rejects the whole request. Source, detail-type, eventBusInvocation, creatorAccount and TargetArn condition context is supported. PutPermission validates policies even with authorization off; organization conditions are unsupported. See [EventBridge bus policies](../architecture/identity.md#eventbridge-bus-policies) for action coverage, rule ARN grants and limitations.

scheduler.title: EventBridge Scheduler
scheduler.summary: Run one-time, rate, and cron schedules against implemented services.
features: Schedule groups and schedule CRUD with time-zone handling
Background runner claims due schedules and invokes targets in-process
Failed deliveries can reach a target SQS dead-letter queue

With authorization on, each run (and the send to the dead-letter queue) assumes the target's role, whose trust policy must allow scheduler.amazonaws.com for the schedule's group (aws:SourceArn) and account, and is decided by the role's identity policies, boundary and the target's resource policy; enforce mode fails the run into the dead-letter path with the denial as ERROR_CODE and ERROR_MESSAGE, soft mode records the check
gaps: No delivery retries; a failed run goes directly to its dead-letter queue
Flexible windows do not delay execution
ECS, SageMaker and CodeBuild templated targets are unsupported
KMS key ARNs are stored without customer-managed encryption
Role sessions are named after the schedule and the denial's error code is the target service's own (such as AccessDeniedException), where AWS reports its own scheduler codes

kinesis.title: Kinesis Data Streams
kinesis.summary: Write and read ordered shard records and feed local Lambda or Firehose consumers.
features: Streams, shards, consumers, shard iterators and record CRUD APIs
Split and merge shard metadata with stable record sequence ordering
Lambda mappings and Firehose sources read records in-process
AWS/Kinesis metrics with dimension StreamName: IncomingRecords and IncomingBytes (PutRecord, PutRecords and DynamoDB streaming destinations) and GetRecords.Records
gaps: No SubscribeToShard enhanced fan-out delivery or throughput enforcement
Resource policies, production record-size settings and warm throughput are outside the subset
KMS encryption settings are stored without encrypting stream records
Kinesis metrics omit shard-level, latency, throughput-exceeded and iterator-age metrics, and GetRecords.Bytes

firehose.title: Data Firehose
firehose.summary: Buffer direct or Kinesis records and deliver them to S3.
features: Delivery streams, tags, direct puts and batch puts
Background buffering and S3 output after size/time thresholds
Kinesis source polling and Lambda processing through the shared caller

With authorization on, S3 writes and Lambda processor calls assume the destination's role, whose trust policy must allow firehose.amazonaws.com for the delivery stream, and are decided by the role's policies; a denied processor call fails its records with Lambda.InvokeAccessDenied and a denied write is recorded as a failed delivery
PutRecord and PutRecordBatch resolve delivery stream ARNs and tags for resource-scoped identity and delivery-role policies
gaps: Only S3 destinations are implemented
No HTTP, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, Snowflake or Iceberg destinations
No MSK/database sources, dynamic partitioning, format conversion, encryption or S3 backup behavior

lambda.title: Lambda
lambda.summary: Manage functions and execute Python/Node locally or managed runtimes in Docker.
features: Function lifecycle, code from ZIP or S3, versions, aliases, layers and tags
ImageConfig EntryPoint, Command and WorkingDirectory round trips for Image functions and overrides Docker startup; Zip functions reject ImageConfig

Provisioned concurrency initializes reusable Docker containers or local Python/Node processes asynchronously with IN_PROGRESS, READY and FAILED status; qualifier pools release on config, alias, version or function deletion, reset and shutdown
Automatic executor selection: Docker when its daemon is reachable, otherwise host Python/Node; lambda.executor can force docker or local
Local Zip execution supports Python 3.x and Node.js CJS/ESM, async/callback handlers, ordered layers, warm reuse, timeouts, logs and directory hot reload
Synchronous Invoke ClientContext accepts base64-encoded JSON and reaches the handler context
LocalStack-compatible hot reload using S3Bucket=hot-reload and an absolute host directory; see [CLI and Terraform examples](../guides/lambda-hot-reload.md)
Synchronous and asynchronous invocation, retries and destinations
SQS, DynamoDB Streams and Kinesis event source mappings
Resource policies, function URLs and concurrency settings
Logs flow into CloudWatch Logs; tests use an in-process fake runtime

AWS-style console for scoped function creation/deletion, ZIP/S3/image deployment, execution roles, runtime/configuration/environment edits, tags, explicit sync/async/dry-run test invocation, SQS trigger settings, DynamoDB stream connections from table pages, SNS subscriptions, paginated CloudWatch logs, and function URL management for $LATEST and aliases with automatic public permissions for NONE URLs
Gateway resource policy enforcement for function-scoped actions, qualified versions/aliases and AWS_IAM function URLs; cross-account full function ARN resolution

With authorization on, SNS, S3 notification, EventBridge and API Gateway Lambda proxy invocations need the function policy (such as AddPermission with a service Principal, SourceArn and SourceAccount) to allow the service principal

With authorization on, Lambda acts as the function's execution role, whose trust policy must allow lambda.amazonaws.com for the function (aws:SourceArn) and account, when it reads an event source (SQS ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage and GetQueueAttributes; Kinesis and DynamoDB stream describe, shard iterator and record reads) and when it sends dead-letter events, asynchronous results and failed stream batches to SQS, SNS, EventBridge or Lambda destinations; CreateEventSourceMapping fails with InvalidParameterValueException in enforce mode when the role cannot read the source, and a mapping whose role loses the permission reports it in LastProcessingResult and stops reading after the cached check expires

DeadLetterConfig on function creation and configuration updates sends discarded asynchronous events to a standard SQS queue or SNS topic as the execution role, with the original event body and RequestID, ErrorCode and ErrorMessage attributes; OnFailure destinations also receive their invocation record

cognitoidp.guide:
## Hosted sign-in

Use `http://localhost:18080/<pool-id>` as the local OIDC issuer. Discovery and JWKS are at
`<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration` and `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json`.
The path form exposes `<issuer>/oauth2/authorize`, `/login`, `/oauth2/token`, `/oauth2/userInfo`,
`/oauth2/revoke`, `/oauth2/idpresponse`, and `/logout`.

With a configured prefix domain, route `<prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com` to TinyStack and send that Host
header; custom domains work the same way. The hosted endpoints then live at the domain root, for example
`https://signin.local.test:18080/oauth2/authorize`. This is Host routing; TinyStack does not provision DNS,
CloudFront, or an ACM certificate. HTTPS clients need an actual TLS listener around the gateway.
The standalone CLI gateway supports optional TLS; see [HTTPS and the local CA](../guides/tls.md). It does not trust forwarded scheme headers.
Discovery remains under `/<pool-id>/.well-known/`; on a configured domain it advertises root hosted endpoints
while retaining the path-form issuer. For HTTP testing, use the path-form issuer on localhost.

Configure an app client with `AllowedOAuthFlowsUserPoolClient=true`, `AllowedOAuthFlows=["code"]`,
`AllowedOAuthScopes`, exact `CallbackURLs`/`LogoutURLs`, and the desired `SupportedIdentityProviders`.
Local sign-in requires `COGNITO`; OIDC providers must exist first. Confidential clients need their secret at the
token endpoint. Public clients can use S256 PKCE. Implicit requires explicit `implicit` enablement.
Callbacks cannot contain fragments. `prompt=login` forces a form, `prompt=none` requires an existing session,
and `login_hint` fills the username field. Browser sessions expire after one hour and are not extended by reuse.

### Amplify

Amplify's redirect implementation constructs HTTPS URLs. Configure a custom domain such as `signin.local.test`
with local DNS and trusted TLS, and a public OAuth client whose callback matches this snippet:

```ts
import { Amplify } from 'aws-amplify';
import { signInWithRedirect } from 'aws-amplify/auth';

Amplify.configure({ Auth: { Cognito: {
  userPoolId: 'us-east-1_POOL',
  userPoolClientId: 'CLIENT_ID',
  loginWith: { oauth: {
    domain: 'signin.local.test:18080',
    scopes: ['openid', 'email', 'profile'],
    redirectSignIn: ['http://localhost:3000/'],
    redirectSignOut: ['http://localhost:3000/'],
    responseType: 'code',
  } },
} } });
await signInWithRedirect();
// For a configured OIDC IdP: signInWithRedirect({ provider: { custom: 'Company' } });
```

See the [Amplify redirect implementation](https://github.com/aws-amplify/amplify-js/blob/main/packages/auth/src/providers/cognito/apis/signInWithRedirect.ts).
API-based password signup and confirmation use the AWS SDK endpoint override separately.

### NextAuth / Auth.js

Register `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/cognito` as a callback for a confidential OAuth client:

```ts
import NextAuth from 'next-auth';
import Cognito from 'next-auth/providers/cognito';

export const { handlers, auth } = NextAuth({ providers: [Cognito({
  clientId: process.env.COGNITO_CLIENT_ID!,
  clientSecret: process.env.COGNITO_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  issuer: 'http://localhost:18080/us-east-1_POOL',
})] });
```

See the [Auth.js Cognito provider](https://authjs.dev/getting-started/providers/cognito).
Other OIDC clients can use the same issuer and its discovery document. HTTP issuer acceptance depends on the
client library's development settings. An external OIDC provider must allow the matching
`<issuer>/oauth2/idpresponse` callback, or the domain-root equivalent. Sign-in creates or reuses
`<ProviderName>_<sub>`; matching email addresses do not automatically link different identities.

Verify mode exposes database metadata inventory; RDS management and full group metadata require signed AWS CLI or SDK requests

DocumentDB and Neptune have no containers, database engine, listeners, MongoDB/graph queries, failover or backup execution; available statuses and endpoints represent records only, even when RDS Docker mode is enabled

Input members outside the generated profile and unsupported enum/filter values fail explicitly

Register/deregister/get/list instances, health status and immediate custom-health changes; service instance revisions update with registrations and health changes

Regional/account-scoped records, resource tags, diagnostic inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API and official-icon console catalogue

CreatorRequestId/UpdaterRequestId replay committed namespace/service/registration/HTTP-update results within the account and Region; changed inputs reject reused tokens

CloudFormation public namespace and advanced properties, and management console pages are unsupported
Unknown filter names/conditions and profile-excluded input members fail explicitly

appconfig.title: AppConfig
appconfig.summary: Manage hosted configuration and deploy it immediately to regional environments.

Binary hosted version creation and retrieval through REST payloads and Content-Type headers; monotonic version numbers, optimistic LatestVersionNumber and unique version labels
All four AWS predefined deployment strategies; builtins are immutable and custom strategies accept LINEAR/EXPONENTIAL growth with ReplicateTo NONE

Start/Get/List/Stop deployments; deployments complete immediately with 100 percent progress, and the environment becomes READY_FOR_DEPLOYMENT; AllowRevert restores the previous hosted version of the latest deployment and marks the environment REVERTED
Inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API; console catalogue entries with official AWS architecture icons

CloudFormation Application, Environment, ConfigurationProfile, HostedConfigurationVersion, DeploymentStrategy and Deployment with selected properties; application/environment/profile/strategy metadata and tags update in place
Regional/account isolation; records, content and sessions persist with SQLite; reset clears all state

Validators are stored records and never executed; AWS.AppConfig.FeatureFlags content is accepted without schema or feature validation
Strategy durations and bake times are metadata; no gradual rollout, monitoring, alarm rollback or background deployment ticker
Extensions, Lambda agent layer, KMS encryption, experiments, account settings and deletion protection checks are unsupported; members outside the profile fail explicitly
StopDeployment requires AllowRevert=true because deployment completes synchronously; only the latest completed deployment can be reverted
Applications and profiles require child deletion first; deleting an environment removes its deployment history; deployed hosted versions cannot be deleted
CloudFormation deletion of Deployment reverts the latest deployment; hosted versions/deployments and trail property changes use replacement; management pages are absent

appconfigdata.title: AppConfig Data
appconfigdata.summary: Poll deployed hosted configuration through configuration session tokens on the same endpoint.
features: StartConfigurationSession resolves application, environment and profile IDs or names in the caller account and Region
GetLatestConfiguration returns binary deployed content on first poll and after a version change, and an empty body on unchanged polls
Opaque random 64-character single-use tokens expire 24 hours after issuance; each poll returns a replacement token and poll interval

Shares appconfig signing name; REST route disambiguation serves /configurationsessions and /configuration alongside control-plane routes

Hosted configurations only; feature-flag evaluation and KMS encryption are unsupported

cloudtrail.title: CloudTrail
cloudtrail.summary: Manage regional trail records and look up external SDK management request history.
features: Trail create/get/describe/update/delete, logging status and start/stop records; S3 destination bucket existence is checked via the S3 service outside transactions
Basic and advanced event selectors are stored trail configuration; selectors do not filter independent event history
Trail tags, inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API, console catalogue and CloudFormation AWS::CloudTrail::Trail with selected properties
Completed external gateway AWS operations generate per-account/Region events whether or not a trail exists or is logging; internal catalog.Caller and console actions are excluded

Event ID/name/source/time, caller access key as Username, ReadOnly, user identity, Region, source IP, user agent, request ID and modeled failure code/message; S3 bucket resources are exposed where routes identify them

LookupEvents supports one EventId, EventName, EventSource, Username, ReadOnly, AccessKeyId, ResourceName or ResourceType attribute, inclusive time range, MaxResults 1–50 and filter-bound cursor pagination newest first
History stores at most the newest 1000 events per account/Region and drops events older than 90 days; persistent storage survives restart and reset clears history
gaps: Trail logging is records only: no S3 log files, digest delivery, CloudWatch Logs delivery, SNS notification, log validation or KMS encryption
Multi-Region and organization trails, shadow trails and IncludeGlobalServiceEvents configuration are unsupported and fail explicitly

Username is the access key rather than resolved IAM user name; resource enrichment currently includes only S3 bucket route labels
History bound is fixed at 1000, not configurable; no CloudTrail Lake, Insights, channels or management console pages
cloudtrail.execution: Trail records / bounded local event history

backup.title: AWS Backup
backup.summary: Persist regional vaults, immutable backup-plan versions and resource-selection metadata without running backups.
features: 17 REST JSON operations for vault CRUD, plan CRUD and version listing, resource-selection CRUD and vault/plan tags
Vault names, stable ARNs and millisecond creation dates; optional same-account/Region KMS key ARN metadata (UUID or multi-Region key ID, not aliases); recovery-point count is always zero

Named plans with 1-10 unique named rules, existing regional target vaults, supported UTC cron expressions, start/completion windows, cold-storage and deletion lifecycle days, and up to 10 RecoveryPointTags per rule

Each update creates an immutable version with a new version ID and creation timestamp; plan IDs/ARNs remain stable and rule IDs are retained for unchanged rule names; exact VersionId retrieval and version pagination

Selections store names, role ARNs, up to 500 unique explicit commercial resource ARNs without wildcards and up to 30 unique STRINGEQUALS tag selectors; explicit resources and selectors can coexist as metadata
Selection IDs are distinct even when display names repeat; at most 100 selections and 10 tag-based selections per plan; plan deletion requires removing selections first
Deleting a plan removes the current version from GetBackupPlan while preserving older version retrieval; ListBackupPlans IncludeDeleted and version lists retain deletion metadata
Regional CreatorRequestId replay for vaults/plans and per-plan replay for selections returns the original creation identity without overwriting records; token/name checks and writes are atomic
Creation tags and atomic TagResource/UntagResource on vaults/plans with shared tag validation and 50-tag limit; paginated ListTags and Resource Groups Tagging API integration
Deterministic ID/name sorting, MaxResults 1-1000, resume-after-deletion cursors bound to account, Region, operation and filter/parent; vault-type/shared and IncludeDeleted filters
Account/Region isolation, SQLite restart and shared reset; generic inventory, official console catalogue icon and Terraform backup endpoint
CloudFormation BackupVault, BackupPlan and BackupSelection selected properties, stable Ref/GetAtt, plan and tag updates, selection replacement, rollback and deletion
gaps: Records only: no schedule execution, resource membership scan, IAM role existence/trust or permission checks, KMS lookup/key creation/encryption, data protection, backup/restore/copy jobs or recovery points

StartBackupJob and job/recovery-point List/Get APIs, vault locks, notifications and access policies, reports, legal holds, organization policies, cross-account runtime and scheduling previews are absent

Plans reject AdvancedBackupSettings, ScanSettings, copy/index/scan actions, continuous backups, air-gapped targets, timezone and archive-opt-in lifecycle members; unsupported members fail explicitly even when set to false or empty arrays
Cron metadata uses the existing parser: six UTC fields with ranges/lists/steps; rate expressions and L/W/# cron syntax are rejected. Omitted schedules default to cron(0 5 ? * * *)

Lifecycle supports days 1-36500 with cold storage at least 90 days before deletion; omit DeleteAfterDays for indefinite retention. Start windows support 60-52560000 minutes, completion windows 1-52560000

Selections reject wildcards, NotResources and Conditions; role/resource ARNs are shape-validated commercial references only and are not resolved; ListOfTags is stored OR-selector metadata without matching resources

Plan names are unique among active plans and support 1-200 alphanumeric/dash/underscore/dot characters; vault names 2-50 without dots, rule/selection/token names 1-50. Plans retain up to 2000 versions; at most 300 vaults and 300 active plans per account/Region

Supplied CreatorRequestId tokens contain 1-50 alphanumeric/dash/underscore/dot characters. Replays return the original create result even after a plan update; vault/selection tokens are removed with their records, plan tokens remain with deletion history
No fabricated default vault or KMS key: create target vaults explicitly; EncryptionKeyArn is absent when omitted. Vault deletion is permitted when empty even if a plan references it

CloudFormation supports BackupVaultName/BackupVaultTags/EncryptionKeyArn, BackupPlan/BackupPlanTags and BackupSelection/BackupPlanId; policy, lock, notifications and all other properties are rejected. Vault name/key changes and selection changes require replacement; no mutation console

config.title: AWS Config
config.summary: Persist regional rule, recorder and delivery-channel metadata without resource capture, compliance evaluation or delivery.
features: 16 AWS JSON 1.1 operations for rule upsert/describe/delete, recorder and delivery-channel configuration/status/lifecycle, and resource tags
Managed rule metadata for REQUIRED_TAGS, S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED, S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_WRITE_PROHIBITED and EC2_INSTANCE_NO_PUBLIC_IP; Source Owner AWS only
Rules retain generated IDs and ARNs on update by name, ID or ARN; description, JSON-object input parameters and resource type/ID or tag scope persist atomically

One customer managed recorder and one delivery channel per account/Region, default names when omitted, same-account role ARN validation, and local S3 destination existence checks
Start/Stop persist requested recorder state and transition timestamps; a delivery channel is required to start and cannot be deleted while the recorder is started
Channel metadata retains S3 bucket/prefix, same-account/Region standard SNS topic ARN and snapshot frequency; no SNS topic lookup or permission evaluation
Creation-only Put tags for rules and recorders, atomic TagResource/UntagResource, deterministic rule pages of 25 and tag pages with Limit 1-100

Account/Region isolation, SQLite reload of configuration/tags/requested state, reset through the shared store, inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API, console catalogue and Terraform configservice endpoint
CloudFormation ConfigRule, ConfigurationRecorder and DeliveryChannel selected properties support create/update/delete; recorder creation leaves requested recording stopped
gaps: Records only: recording=true represents requested control-plane state, not active resource capture; lastStatus and recording-event results are absent
Delivery status returns the channel name without history, snapshot or stream results; no S3/SNS writes, background delivery, compliance evaluation, Lambda invocation or remediation
CUSTOM_LAMBDA/CUSTOM_POLICY, SourceDetails, custom policy details, rule lifecycle state writes, MaximumExecutionFrequency and evaluation modes are unsupported

Service-linked recorders, recording modes/overrides, exclusion/recording strategies, connector fields and explicit resource types outside the four listed types are unsupported; allSupported is metadata only
KMS delivery, cross-account/Region SNS ARNs, FIFO SNS topics, aggregators, conformance packs, organization Config and external resource gathering are unsupported
Names are limited to letters, digits, hyphens and underscores (rules 1-128, recorder/channel 1-256); rule rename requires delete/create and singleton names cannot change until deletion
IAM role existence/trust, bucket policies and delivery permissions are not evaluated; destination bucket must already exist locally in the caller's account

CloudFormation omits Compliance, EvaluationModes, MaximumExecutionFrequency, recording modes, StartedOnCreate and KMS properties; no automatic start, capture or delivery. Explicit DependsOn is needed from channel to recorder
Delivery channels have no AWS resource ARN or tags; their metadata appears in generic inventory, while tag APIs support rules and recorders only; no mutation console pages

account.title: AWS Account
account.summary: Read-only account metadata, primary contact details, and region opt-in statuses for the calling account.

Multi-account caller isolation rejecting malformed (including explicit empty string) or cross-account AccountId without Organizations delegation

Read-only/records-only first slice: mutation operations like EnableRegion, DisableRegion, PutContactInformation, and AlternateContact APIs are not implemented

Account has no ordinary resource lifecycle or mutation UI; no CloudFormation resource types are registered

wafv2.title: WAF v2
wafv2.summary: Persist scoped web ACLs, IP sets, rule groups, tags and regional association metadata without inspecting traffic.

Stable names, UUIDs, resource ARNs and internal creation timestamps; descriptions, Allow/Block DefaultAction, VisibilityConfig booleans and metric names, declared immutable RuleGroup Capacity and selected Rules persist atomically

IPV4 and IPV6 CIDRs, including individual /32 and /128 addresses, empty address arrays and all nonzero prefix lengths; at most 10000 addresses, with atomic family/range validation and immutable family

Get/List/Create return current configuration LockToken; Update/Delete compare tokens and write/rotate in one serializable store transaction, with exactly one concurrent winner for a shared old token; tokens survive SQLite restart and tag/association changes
Association replacement, idempotent disassociation, empty GetWebACLForResource when unassociated and sorted ListResourcesForWebACL; default APPLICATION_LOAD_BALANCER or explicit API_GATEWAY filters

List and tag pagination use Limit 1-100 and cursors bound to account, Region, operation and WAF scope or ARN; resources sort by name/UUID and tags by key, with resume after deletion

CloudFormation AWS::WAFv2::WebACL, IPSet, RuleGroup and WebACLAssociation selected properties; name|id|scope Ref, Arn/Id GetAtt on configuration resources, live lock-token fetch for update/delete, tag replacement at 50 tags, compensation and stack rollback; shared reset clears all WAF records
gaps: Records only: no request evaluation, filtering, ingress integration, network enforcement, sampled requests, CloudWatch metrics, CAPTCHA/challenges, logging engine or runtime counters; VisibilityConfig is stored requested metadata

Only aws commercial partition and the finite commercial Region allowlist in internal/services/wafv2/service.go; CLOUDFRONT outside us-east-1 fails. Global associations through CloudFront distribution workflows are not implemented

These are format-only metadata, without owning-service lookup; accountless API Gateway ARNs are stored under the caller account

Rule-group Capacity is declared metadata (1-5000), preserved by updates; no WCU estimation, capacity consumption output or CheckCapacity. At most 50 direct reference rules per ACL/group and 100 records of each type per account/Region/scope

Names support 1-128 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen. Descriptions use the exact pinned pattern and 256-character limit; metric names use the pinned pattern and 1-255 limit, excluding All and Default_Action. IPv4-mapped IPv6 CIDRs are rejected; CIDRs are preserved as supplied

Update requests provide complete selected desired state; omitted description/rules clear those fields. Family and capacity cannot be updated through the WAF APIs. Deleting referenced IP sets/groups or associated ACLs returns WAFAssociatedItemException

CloudFormation properties are Name/Scope/Description/Tags plus Addresses/IPAddressVersion for IPSet, Rules/VisibilityConfig/Capacity for RuleGroup, Rules/VisibilityConfig/DefaultAction for WebACL, and ResourceArn/WebACLArn for associations. Configuration name/scope and IP family/group capacity changes require replacement; Arn and Id are the only configuration GetAtt attributes

CloudFormation tag updates are a local extension to the AWS documentation creation-only note: unrelated live tags remain, removals free capacity before replacement and failed tag/configuration calls compensate. No mutation console or additional WAFv2 resources

efs.title: Amazon EFS
efs.summary: Persist regional file-system, mount-target and access-point metadata without a mountable NFS filesystem.
features: 15 REST JSON operations for file-system CRUD, mount-target CRUD/security-group replacement, access-point CRUD and resource tags; SDK signing name elasticfilesystem from the pinned model

Stable fs/fsmt/fsap IDs, filesystem/access-point ARNs, creation tokens, account/Region ownership, encryption/KMS metadata, performance and throughput configuration, POSIX user/root metadata and creation tags

FileSystemAlreadyExists and AccessPointAlreadyExists return original identifiers on token reuse without mutating initial records, including conflicting retries; tokens are scoped to account/Region and removed with records

Locally available metadata defaults: generalPurpose performance, bursting throughput, Encrypted=false, zero size/usage values and a fixed creation-time size timestamp. Mount-target count reflects stored records; no real data storage is represented

Atomic throughput updates with bursting/provisioned/elastic modes, provisioned 1-3414 MiBps including fractions; maxIO cannot use elastic. Identity, immutable settings and previous state survive failed updates

Existing scoped EC2 subnet/group lookup in the same transaction; no default VPC seeding or EC2 changes. One VPC per filesystem and one target per local AZ; IPv4 CIDR validation and deterministic unused EFS metadata addresses; at most five unique groups

Access points persist UID/GID, up to 16 secondary groups and optional root path/creation owner/mode settings. IDs are 0-4294967295, paths at most four non-dot-prefixed components and 100 Unicode characters; modes 3-4 octal digits

Filesystem/access-point references accept IDs or same-account/Region commercial ARNs; mount targets accept IDs only. Both mount targets and access points must be deleted before their filesystem; dependency errors preserve all state

Validated unique tags, modeled lengths/character sets/reserved prefixes and 50-tag limit; deterministic sorted retrieval, inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API filters elasticfilesystem:file-system/access-point
Scoped/filter-bound deterministic pagination with default 100 and positive requested sizes capped at 1000; stable ID/key order and resume after cursor deletion

SQLite restart, offline export/import fixtures and shared reset retain exact identifiers/configuration/relations/tokens; default app assembly, verified SigV4, resource browser, official console icon and Terraform efs endpoint

CloudFormation FileSystem/MountTarget/AccessPoint Ref/GetAtt, mutable throughput/security-group/tag updates and immutable replacement. EFS-specific retirement orders children first and restores original incarnations during rollback; 50-tag replacement and failed-tag compensation preserve unrelated tags
gaps: Records only: no NFS server, mount listener, mountable filesystem, filesystem bytes, POSIX execution, EC2 interfaces or real IP allocation, IAM/KMS evaluation, backup/replication/lifecycle jobs or throughput cooldown/capacity simulation

CreateFileSystem supports CreationToken/PerformanceMode/Encrypted/KmsKeyId/ThroughputMode/ProvisionedThroughputInMibps/Tags; AvailabilityZoneName (One Zone), Backup and FileSystemProtection are excluded. Shared decoder rejects unsupported members as NotImplemented even when false/null/empty

KmsKeyId accepts UUID/mrk IDs, aliases and same-account/Region commercial key/alias ARNs as format-only metadata; omitted KmsKeyId remains absent, even for encrypted records. No default KMS key or ARN is fabricated

CreateMountTarget supports FileSystemId/SubnetId/IpAddress/IpAddressType=IPV4_ONLY/SecurityGroups. EC2 has IPv4 subnets only: IPv6/DUAL_STACK and Ipv6Address are rejected. NetworkInterfaceId is omitted. Metadata address checks cover EFS records only, not EC2 instances/interfaces; EC2 deletion has no EFS dependency guard

Creation defaults to the existing VPC default security group when no groups are provided. ModifyMountTargetSecurityGroups replaces the list; an empty list clears it. AZ names/IDs come directly from local EC2 subnet records

CreateAccessPoint supports ClientToken/FileSystemId/PosixUser/RootDirectory/Tags including every selected nested member. Omitted root path defaults to /; optional CreationInfo requires all its fields. No paths/users/groups are created or verified on disk
Tokens contain 1-64 printable ASCII characters; at most 1000 filesystems per account/Region and 10000 access points per filesystem, without adjustable quotas

CloudFormation FileSystem: Encrypted/KmsKeyId/PerformanceMode/ThroughputMode/ProvisionedThroughputInMibps/FileSystemTags; MountTarget: FileSystemId/SubnetId/IpAddress/IpAddressType/SecurityGroups; AccessPoint: FileSystemId/ClientToken/PosixUser/RootDirectory/AccessPointTags. Unsupported properties are rejected

Immutable filesystem settings, mount placement/address and access-point token/POSIX/root settings require replacement. Reusing an explicit access-point token or creating a replacement mount in an occupied AZ/address fails safely with rollback; change the token/placement/address as needed
No dedicated mutation console. Follow the [executable records workflow](../guides/efs-records.md) for exact supported members, defaults, reference rules and CLI commands

batch.title: AWS Batch
batch.summary: Persist regional compute-environment, queue and revisioned container-definition metadata without provisioning or running jobs.
features: 14 REST JSON metadata operations: compute environment and queue CRUD, definition registration/description/deregistration and resource tags

UNMANAGED and finite x86 MANAGED EC2 records must be created ENABLED (omitted state defaults to ENABLED); explicit DISABLED creation returns ClientException/400 without storing a record. Updates accept ENABLED/DISABLED; VALID describes local metadata, with no fabricated ECS cluster or runtime identifiers

Managed capacity/configuration retains vCPU bounds, desired capacity, instance choices, instance profile and actual scoped EC2 subnet/security-group references; all network lookups share the storage transaction

Job definitions preserve monotonically increasing scoped revisions and revisioned ARNs, active/inactive history, container image/command, legacy CPU/memory or VCPU/MEMORY requirements, environment, role and parameter metadata
Atomic writes and failed mutations, account/Region isolation, deterministic filter-bound pagination and concurrent registration/name uniqueness
Tags are scoped to each resource ARN and definition revision, with 50-key merge limits, inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API support
SQLite restart, offline fixture export/import into a fresh store followed by normal restart, shared reset, verified SigV4, official console icon and Terraform batch endpoint

CloudFormation ComputeEnvironment, JobQueue and JobDefinition selected properties with correct ARN Ref/GetAtt, queue dependency updates, definition revision replacement and original-incarnation rollback. Removed template tags free capacity before additions; failed additions compensate live removed values
gaps: Records only: no SubmitJob/DescribeJobs/ListJobs/CancelJob/TerminateJob, scheduler, Docker/ECS/EKS jobs, provisioning/autoscaling, image pulls, IAM role existence/trust/permissions or execution readiness. VALID means valid local metadata

Only MANAGED EC2 or UNMANAGED are supported. Managed x86 choices are finite c5/m5/r5 families/sizes, optimal and default_x86_64; Fargate, Spot, ARM, EKS, ECS managed instances, launch templates, custom AMIs, instance tags, scaling policies and infrastructure updates are excluded

Create environment supports name/type/state/serviceRole/tags and selected computeResources. Both types require ENABLED at creation (also the omitted-state default); DISABLED returns ClientException/400 without storing a record. Update accepts ENABLED/DISABLED and supports state/serviceRole and minvCpus/maxvCpus/desiredvCpus only. Desired capacity cannot decrease or leave the retained bounds; bounds alone do not invoke a scheduler

Definitions support container/EC2 only; retry/timeout, GPU, multinode, volumes, secrets, privileges, EKS/ECS advanced properties and tag propagation are absent. Unsupported inputs fail explicitly including false/null/empty

Descriptions default to all definition statuses and return all matching revisions, rather than latest active name resolution. Explicit definition lists require revisioned identifiers and cannot combine with other parameters. Inactive history is retained indefinitely locally
Scheduling policies, fair-share capacity, service environments, consumable resources and advanced queue actions are future scope

CloudFormation supports name/type/state/serviceRole/computeResources/tags for environments, name/state/priority/order/tags for queues and name/type/parameters/container/platform/tags for definitions. Compute config/role/type/name changes replace the environment; definition metadata changes create another revision and retire the previous revision after success
