costandusagereportservice.summary: Store legacy CUR report definitions and tags as account-wide records without generating billing data or report files.
features: All seven pinned AWS JSON 1.1 operations: PutReportDefinition, DescribeReportDefinitions, ModifyReportDefinition, DeleteReportDefinition, TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource
Round-trip destination, time unit, format, compression, schema elements, additional artifacts, refresh preferences and report versioning with model validation
Unique case-sensitive report names, immutable names on modification, ordered pagination with the pinned model page size of five, and account isolation across signing Regions
Native tags with the 50-tag limit, Resource Groups Tagging API integration, console inventory with RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false, and CUR us-east-1 definition ARNs
AWS Go SDK v2 lifecycle, persistence and reset coverage; Terraform aws_cur_report_definition apply, refresh, update, import and destroy coverage using the cur endpoint override
Account-wide console for report definition creation, modification, deletion and tags; S3 destination, format, compression, time unit, schema and artifact settings
gaps: Records only: no AWS bills, cost calculations, cost fixtures, report files, manifests, S3 writes, Athena/Redshift/QuickSight integrations or delivery status
S3 destination existence, ownership and delivery permissions are not validated; AWS documents destination validation separately and ownership checks at delivery
BillingViewArn and ReportStatus inputs explicitly return ValidationException; Billing Conductor views and report delivery are not implemented
No report-count quota is enforced; only modeled input constraints and the shared tag limit are enforced
No CloudFormation handler for AWS::CUR::ReportDefinition; CDK and awscc deployment are unsupported
CUR 2.0 and BCM Data Exports are not implemented

budgets.title: AWS Budgets
budgets.summary: Manage account-wide budgets and deliver supported ACTUAL alerts from user-supplied USD cost fixtures.
features: Sixteen AWS JSON 1.1 operations: budget CRUD/list, notification CRUD/list, subscriber CRUD/list and native tags
Account-wide definitions shared across signing Regions, account identity checks, empty-Region budget ARNs and encoded storage names
Fixed and planned limits, filters/types and time periods stored as configuration; supported COST/USD calendar budgets expose fixture-backed ActualSpend
CreateBudget accepts notifications with subscribers; notification identity excludes NotificationState and defaults ThresholdType to PERCENTAGE
AWS-documented limits of five notifications and ten EMAIL plus one SNS subscriber per notification; duplicate definitions fail explicitly
Ordered pagination, inventory with evaluation readiness and notification state, Resource Groups Tagging API integration and Terraform aws_budgets_budget lifecycle
Account-wide console for fixed COST/USAGE budget creation, limit edits, notification and email/SNS subscriber management, tags and deletion
MONTHLY/QUARTERLY/ANNUALLY actual spend with supported dimension filters; no fixture data returns zero; see guides/costs.md
One-second ACTUAL evaluation reuses ActualSpend; exact decimal percentage/absolute thresholds and GREATER_THAN/LESS_THAN/EQUAL_TO comparisons
Durable once-per-rule-per-period markers, ALARM/OK state and bounded at-least-once delivery retries survive persistent-storage restarts
Same-account standard SNS topics use their own Region; direct EMAIL is captured in deliveries and messages as service budgets; reset clears markers and delivery jobs
gaps: No forecasts or price estimation; FORECASTED notifications are retained but never fire. Explicit CostTypes, unsupported filters, other budget types and non-USD budgets are stored without evaluation
Budget actions, performance history, account notification history, auto-adjustment, billing views and modern filter expressions/metrics are unsupported
No CloudFormation handlers: AWS::Budgets::Budget and AWS::Budgets::BudgetsAction, CDK and awscc deployment are unavailable
Local one-second cadence differs from AWS billing refresh; planned limits use the latest timestamp not after evaluation time and carry forward; percentage alerts wait for an applicable limit
EMAIL is capture only; standard same-account SNS only; SNS topic policies are not enforced; SNS acceptance does not guarantee downstream delivery
Four delivery attempts with local 1/2/4-second backoff and a one-minute crash lease; final failures retained in storage; recent delivery/message diagnostics are in memory
Alert text approximates AWS plain-text notifications; no AWS HTML template, account masking, unsubscribe link or budget actions; completed jobs and markers are retained until budget deletion or reset
budgets.execution: Fixture-backed actual spend and ACTUAL notifications

opensearchserverless.title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
opensearchserverless.summary: Manage collection and security policy records; no search data plane is served.
features: Collection create, batch get, filtered list, description update and delete; SEARCH, TIMESERIES and VECTORSEARCH with standby replicas and deterministic CREATING → ACTIVE and DELETING transitions on reads

Encryption and network security policy CRUD, data access policy CRUD, JSON shape validation, optimistic policy versions, resource filters and pagination; matching encryption policy required for collection creation
Collection ARN tags, Resource Groups Tagging API, Resource Groups collection type, inventory and console; account capacity settings and policy counts
Client-token replay and parameter conflict detection for collection and policy writes; Terraform collection, security policy and access policy coverage
gaps: Records only, no search data plane: collection and dashboard endpoints have AWS-shaped URLs but serve no data, indexes, queries or dashboard
No VPC endpoints or SAML security configurations; no provisioning or EC2 networking integration; network sources and IAM/KMS principals are syntax-checked metadata, not authorization or connectivity
No collection groups, vector options, deletion protection, lifecycle policies or data plane operations; unsupported request members are rejected
Reads return the current collection lifecycle state then advance it; inventory does not advance state; idempotency records persist until reset
Capacity settings are records only and do not allocate or meter OCUs; no quota enforcement

databasemigrationservice.title: AWS Database Migration Service
databasemigrationservice.summary: Store replication subnet groups, instances, endpoints and tasks as records only, with no data migration.
features: Twenty-two pinned AWS JSON 1.1 operations with dms signing, SDK v2 CRUD, lifecycle and Terraform coverage for all four resource types

Subnet groups validate existing TinyStack EC2 subnets in the same VPC across at least two Availability Zones; instances validate VPC security groups and retain class, engine, storage, MultiAZ and public accessibility metadata

Instances return creating then available on Describe observations; reboot returns rebooting then available. Task observations advance creating to ready, starting to running, and full-load running to stopped with a simulated completion reason

Endpoint engine settings are retained for common relational, S3, DynamoDB, Kinesis, Kafka, document and other supported engines; passwords are never persisted or returned and endpoint inspector bodies are redacted
Task migration type and table mapping JSON shape validation, source/target endpoint type checks, lifecycle guards and dependency-aware deletes
Describe filters and Marker/MaxRecords pagination (20–100, default 100), native ARN tags with shared limits, Resource Groups Tagging API integration, scoped inventory and console listing
gaps: Records only, no data migration: no replication compute, connectivity tests, table statistics, logs, CDC checkpoints, network allocation or real completion is claimed
Certificates, event subscriptions, account attributes, serverless replication configurations and other DMS APIs are not implemented

Instance modifications apply to metadata synchronously, including deferred requests; maintenance windows are metadata, not scheduled. Engine versions and classes are checked syntactically rather than against a regional catalog
A replication subnet group must be explicitly supplied when creating an instance. No IP addresses or KMS keys are provisioned

Endpoint settings are metadata only; nested authentication fields, certificate references, exact settings replacement and DMS Transfer settings are rejected. Top-level and nested passwords and other Smithy-sensitive settings are accepted and discarded
Task CDC start/stop positions and timestamps, task data, custom resource identifiers and Kerberos settings are unsupported. Table mappings are checked for structural validity, not evaluated
Transitions advance only for the returned Describe page; inventory and tag reads do not advance them. Full-load completion is simulated and moves no data
No CloudFormation resource provider

kinesisanalyticsv2.title: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
kinesisanalyticsv2.summary: Store Managed Flink applications, configuration, versions and snapshots without running jobs.
features: Twenty AWS JSON 1.1 operations: application create/describe/list/update/delete/start/stop, describe/list versions, add/delete VPC and CloudWatch logging configuration, create/describe/list/delete snapshots and three native tag operations
FLINK-1_6, FLINK-1_8, FLINK-1_11, FLINK-1_13, FLINK-1_15, FLINK-1_18, FLINK-1_19 and FLINK-1_20 runtimes from the pinned model; STREAMING mode only

Deterministic READY to STARTING to RUNNING and RUNNING to STOPPING to READY lifecycle; updates enter UPDATING, preserve the final running state, increment the version and retain historical configuration; Force stop accepts READY
Optimistic CurrentApplicationVersionId checks, timestamp-guarded application and snapshot deletion with whole-second creation timestamps, scoped pagination, account and Region isolation
Text and ZIP code records with size limits and MD5 metadata; S3 code objects must exist in TinyStack; environment properties, Flink checkpoint, monitoring and parallelism configuration
VPC subnet and security group existence and VPC consistency checks through TinyStack EC2; CloudWatch logging options require an existing scoped TinyStack log stream
User snapshots require RUNNING and contain READY metadata with the application version; tag limits, inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API and console integration
IAM role ARN validation and gateway PassRole checks for CreateApplication and UpdateApplication; Terraform application and snapshot coverage
gaps: Records only, no Flink runtime: no jobs, workers, networking, checkpoints, restore, logs, metrics or results are executed or produced

DescribeApplication returns the current lifecycle state then advances it; DELETING removes the application after that read; lists and inventory do not advance state; snapshots contain no job state and normal stop creates no automatic snapshot

SQL-1_0, Zeppelin Studio notebooks and FLINK-2_x runtimes are explicitly rejected; SQL inputs/outputs, interactive sessions, maintenance, rollback, encryption, conditional tokens and operation history are unsupported
IAM role existence and trust are not checked by the service; environment and runtime settings are metadata, not resource allocation
No CloudFormation provider; application deletion accepts READY or RUNNING and removes snapshot and version history; S3 validation reads the object before the application transaction

signer.title: AWS Signer
signer.summary: Store signing profiles, permissions and jobs with illustrative S3 artifacts.
features: Seventeen REST JSON operations: five fixed signing platforms, versioned profiles, cancellation and revocation, optimistic permission revisions, signing jobs and tags
Profile status and platform filters, pagination, signature validity periods, account and Region isolation; IoT signing certificates must exist in scoped TinyStack ACM
S3 source bucket/key/version validation and synchronous destination writes; idempotent job tokens, job filters and signature revocation records
Inventory, Resource Groups tagging, console and Terraform signing profile, profile permission and signing job coverage
gaps: Artifacts append a TinyStack signature envelope to source bytes. Signatures are not cryptographically verifiable by AWS tooling; ZIP files are not actually signed.
SignPayload, GetRevocationStatus, Notation registry signing, platform overrides and signing parameters are unsupported.
Permissions are stored policy metadata; cross-account delegation is not executed. GetSigningProfile has no policy revision field in the AWS model; ListProfilePermissions returns revisions.
Lambda CodeSigningConfig is not implemented; Lambda currently reports no code signing configuration. No Lambda profile validation integration.
Jobs finish synchronously; S3 failures are retained as Failed jobs. Revocation is metadata only and does not modify S3 output. Interrupted jobs remain InProgress; no restart worker.
No certificate key-usage or algorithm validation, trust verification, IAM permission enforcement by Signer, CloudFormation provider or AWS cryptographic signing.

waf.title: WAF Classic
waf.summary: Store global WAF Classic control-plane records only, with no request filtering.
features: 65 AWS JSON 1.1 operations, target AWSWAF_20150824 and signing name waf; global account-scoped records independent of WAFv2
GetChangeToken and GetChangeTokenStatus; single-use tokens consumed atomically with successful mutations and deterministic PROVISIONED, PENDING, INSYNC transitions on status reads

Create/Get/List/Update/Delete IPSet, ByteMatchSet, SizeConstraintSet, SqlInjectionMatchSet, XssMatchSet, GeoMatchSet, RegexPatternSet and RegexMatchSet; INSERT/DELETE updates, duplicate and absent-member errors, CIDR and tuple validation
Regular and rate-based rules with validated same-account condition references, immutable metrics, IP rate keys and rate limit metadata; GetRateBasedRuleManagedKeys returns empty
Web ACLs with ALLOW/BLOCK defaults and prioritized REGULAR/RATE_BASED rules with ALLOW/BLOCK/COUNT actions; nonempty and referenced-resource delete guards
Creation tags on rules, rate-based rules and web ACLs; TagResource/UntagResource/ListTagsForResource, shared WAFv2 tag validation, inventory, Resource Groups types and generic tagging
Terraform aws_waf_ipset, aws_waf_byte_match_set, aws_waf_rule, aws_waf_rate_based_rule and aws_waf_web_acl apply/update/destroy coverage
Put/Get/Delete/ListLoggingConfigurations store web ACL logging metadata, validate an existing owned us-east-1 Firehose stream named aws-waf-logs-*, and retain redacted fields; no log delivery
gaps: Records only, no request filtering, request evaluation, enforcement, metrics, sampled requests or rate counters; regex strings are stored verbatim without executing or validating against an AWS regex engine
WAF Regional, ALB/API Gateway associations, rule groups, managed rule subscriptions and permission policies are unsupported
No CloudFront association integration or CloudFormation resource handlers; resource changes require unused change tokens, while tag and logging APIs follow their token-free AWS request shapes
List cursors use resource IDs and tags use keys; Limit is 1-100. Classic IPv4 ranges support /8 and /16-/32, IPv6 /24,/32,/48,/56,/64,/128; names are immutable

emr.title: Amazon EMR
emr.summary: Records only, no Hadoop/Spark runtime: store classic EMR clusters, synthetic capacity and simulated steps.
features: Thirty-three JSON 1.1 ElasticMapReduce operations with elasticmapreduce signing: cluster creation, describe/list, termination protection, visibility, concurrency and termination
Instance group auto-scaling policies (put, remove, list) and cluster managed scaling policies (put, get, remove); records only, scaling never executes
Account and Region block public access configuration (get, put) with default permitted rule ranges; records only, security group rules are not enforced
Read-driven STARTING → BOOTSTRAPPING → RUNNING → WAITING and TERMINATING → TERMINATED transitions with reasons and timestamps; clusters without keep-alive terminate after all steps finish

Fixed EMR 6.x and 7.x release labels, application/configuration metadata, EC2 subnet and security group existence/VPC validation, IAM service role and instance profile role validation, S3 log bucket validation and security configuration references; release list includes EMR 7.14.0
Instance group and fleet add/list/resize, synthetic instance IDs and subnet private addresses, bootstrap action metadata; no compute is allocated
Step submission, describe/list filters and cancellation; simulated PENDING → RUNNING → COMPLETED without executing scripts; ActionOnFailure concurrency validation and failure policy handling

Security configuration create/describe/list/delete with JSON validation, cluster tags with shared limits, inventory, Resource Groups integration, console and Terraform cluster/security configuration/instance group coverage
Cluster state and creation time filters, step ID/state filters and Marker pagination with 50 records per page; account and Region isolation; idle auto-termination evaluated on reads
gaps: No Hadoop/Spark runtime, EC2 provisioning, bootstrap or JAR execution, logs, output, metrics, billing or actual failures; successful steps always complete and cancellation does not invoke failure policies
State transitions and idle timeout checks advance on DescribeCluster, ListClusters, DescribeStep and ListSteps; inventory and capacity reads do not advance execution
Studios, notebooks, sessions, EBS configuration, custom AMIs and legacy AMI cluster creation are unsupported and rejected

Ec2KeyName and application/configuration properties are metadata; security configuration JSON is stored without interpreting encryption settings; synthetic instances do not exist in the EC2 API; UnhealthyNodeReplacement and EbsOptimized are metadata only
Security groups require an explicit subnet; synthetic capacity is limited to 1000 instances per group/fleet; weighted fleet capacity is approximated with the first configured instance type
AutoTerminationPolicy is accepted on RunJobFlow and readable through GetAutoTerminationPolicy; separate policy mutations and CloudFormation resource providers are unsupported

bedrock.title: Amazon Bedrock
bedrock.summary: Browse a fixed model catalogue and manage local inference profiles, guardrails and logging configuration.
features: Eighteen REST JSON operations: foundation model listing and details, provider/modality/inference filters, system and application inference profiles, guardrail drafts and immutable versions, invocation logging configuration and tags
Idempotent create tokens, list pagination, account and Region isolation, resource inventory and Resource Groups tagging
Fixed real model IDs for Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan and Nova, Meta Llama and Cohere Embed; model/profile ID and ARN resolution for local inference
gaps: Catalogue metadata is a fixed snapshot, independent of live regional availability and model access entitlements. Runtime inputs support text only, even when catalogue models also support images or video.
Guardrails implement only custom literal word policies through ApplyGuardrail. Topic/content/sensitive-information policies, KMS, managed words and automatic invocation guardrails are unsupported.
Invocation logging configuration is stored only; no CloudWatch/S3 log delivery. No training, customization, provisioning, model import or CloudFormation handlers.

bedrockruntime.title: Amazon Bedrock Runtime
bedrockruntime.scope: Account and Region; fixtures are default-account-wide
bedrockruntime.summary: Return predictable text, tool-use fixtures and hash-derived embeddings without network calls.
features: Six REST JSON operations: InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream, Converse, ConverseStream, CountTokens and ApplyGuardrail
Provider-native Anthropic messages, Titan text/embeddings, Nova messages, Llama prompts and Cohere embeddings; normalized deterministic vectors, usage estimates and maximum-token truncation

AWS event-stream response frames flushed individually: provider-native Anthropic, Titan, Nova and Llama text deltas with invocation metrics; ConverseStream message/block lifecycle, tool-use fixtures, usage and latency metadata
Default reply is TinyStack: followed by the last user message. Stored substring/regex fixtures select text, stop reason and optional Converse tool use; reset clears fixtures
Control-plane model IDs, system profile IDs/ARNs and application profile IDs/ARNs resolve locally; unknown identifiers and unsupported request fields fail explicitly
gaps: No bidirectional streaming or asynchronous inference. Response streaming is deterministic and finite; embedding models reject native response streaming. No simulated mid-stream model failures.

Only text inputs and declared token limits are supported. Sampling controls, multimodal inputs, prompt management, reasoning and tool-result conversations are unsupported. Tool-use fixtures require a matching Converse toolConfig.
Token counts are whitespace-word estimates; latencyMs is zero. Embeddings are SHA-256-derived test vectors, not semantic embeddings. No real model inference or network access.
ApplyGuardrail performs case-insensitive literal substring matching of custom words only; it is explicitly invoked and does not run automatically during inference.

elasticbeanstalk.title: Elastic Beanstalk
elasticbeanstalk.summary: Manage applications, source versions, configuration templates and simulated environments.
features: 32 AWS Query operations for application and version lifecycles, lifecycle policy records, environments, configuration templates, options, platform discovery, events, DNS names, tags and storage locations
Eight fixed Amazon Linux 2023 platforms: Node.js, Python, Java Corretto, Docker, Go, .NET, PHP and Ruby; platform filters and paginated versions, environments, events and platforms

Background Launching/Updating to Ready and Terminating to Terminated transitions, 1-hour retention and purge of terminated environments and events, synthetic Green/Ok health and resource records, CNAME reservations and swaps
S3 source existence check when Process=true, optional source deletion, S3 storage bucket creation, account and Region isolation, shared inventory, Resource Groups and console integration
gaps: Environments are records only. No application code is deployed or executed; no EC2, load balancer, Auto Scaling or SQS resources are provisioned, and CNAMEs do not resolve to a runtime.
Process=true checks S3 object existence only; source archives and .ebextensions are not parsed or built. Unprocessed source bundles are stored without an object check.

Lifecycle policy settings are stored metadata; automatic version expiry, IAM role evaluation and retention jobs are not executed (terminated environments expire after 1 hour, but application versions are retained indefinitely).

Fixed platform catalogue and a limited configuration option subset; no custom platforms, CodeCommit/CodeBuild/image sources, source-configuration cloning, operations roles, logs or real health metrics.

rdsdata.title: RDS Data API
rdsdata.summary: Execute SQL through the AWS Data API against local Aurora Docker engines.
features: ExecuteStatement, BatchExecuteStatement, BeginTransaction, CommitTransaction and RollbackTransaction use database/sql with PostgreSQL and MySQL drivers outside storage transactions
resourceArn resolves a same-account/Region Aurora cluster with its HTTP endpoint enabled; secretArn must resolve a Secrets Manager JSON secret whose username and password match the cluster
Database and schema selection, named parameters with string, long, double, boolean, blob and null Fields, and DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP/DECIMAL/UUID/JSON type hints
Typed result Fields, optional column metadata, formatRecordsAs=JSON formattedRecords, affected row counts and MySQL generated IDs; PostgreSQL generated values use SQL RETURNING
Transactions remain in memory per cluster, expire after three minutes idle or 24 hours total, and roll back on cluster stop, reset or service shutdown

SQL failures preserve the database message in BadRequestException; missing clusters return NotFoundException, disabled HTTP endpoints return HttpEndpointNotEnabledException, invalid credentials return ForbiddenException, and records mode reports that no engine is running
gaps: Requires rds.instances: docker for SQL execution; no SQL interpreter or canned results in records mode
Array parameters/results, resultSetOptions, continueAfterTimeout, cancellation and asynchronous execution are unsupported; unimplemented input members fail explicitly
Cluster credentials are validated locally; IAM database authentication, AWS connection management, network failover and distributed transactions are not emulated
Column metadata reflects database/sql driver information; table/schema provenance and auto-increment metadata are unavailable; operations are serialized within the Data API service
Transactions and SQL connection state are not persisted across TinyStack restarts

apigatewaymanagementapi.title: API Gateway Management API
apigatewaymanagementapi.summary: Send to, inspect and close live API Gateway WebSocket connections.
features: PostToConnection, GetConnection and DeleteConnection through AWS SDK v2 at execute-api /<stage>/@connections/<connection-id> endpoints, including TinyStack path-style endpoints
Connection details include connected/last-active timestamps, source IP and user agent; server push delivers text messages and DeleteConnection closes the socket and invokes $disconnect

Connection lookup is scoped by account, Region, API and stage; unknown or closed connections return GoneException (410); management requests use SigV4 callers and execute-api:ManageConnections authorization
PostToConnection rejects payloads larger than 128 KiB with PayloadTooLargeException
gaps: Connections exist only in memory while their sockets are open; they are not persisted or listed as separate inventory resources
No binary message delivery, per-frame AWS quota emulation or management API throttling

securityhub.title: AWS Security Hub
securityhub.summary: Store regional Security Hub hubs, standard subscriptions, ASFF findings, custom insights and action targets over REST JSON without security evaluation.
features: Twenty-three pinned-model operations for hub lifecycle/configuration, standards, ASFF findings, insights, custom actions and hub tags; disabled hubs return InvalidAccessException; disabling a hub synchronously removes all its regional records

Fixed catalogue: AWS Foundational Security Best Practices v1.0.0, CIS AWS Foundations v1.2.0/v1.4.0/v3.0.0, PCI DSS v3.2.1 and NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5. AWS ARNs from https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/securityhub/describe-standards.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark.html; CIS 1.2.0 uses arn:aws:securityhub:::ruleset/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/1.2.0, others use arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/<standard>/v/<version>, including nist-800-53/v/5.0.0

Catalogue ARNs (replace <region>): arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/aws-foundational-security-best-practices/v/1.0.0; arn:aws:securityhub:::ruleset/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/1.2.0; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/1.4.0; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/cis-aws-foundations-benchmark/v/3.0.0; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/pci-dss/v/3.2.1; arn:aws:securityhub:<region>::standards/nist-800-53/v/5.0.0

EnableDefaultStandards defaults to true and enables AWS Foundational Security Best Practices v1.0.0 and CIS v1.2.0, matching https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-settingup.html. Subscriptions become READY immediately and disappear synchronously on disable (response status DELETING)
Every input is checked against the model's required, length, range, pattern and enum constraints and fails InvalidInputException; BatchImportFindings checks each finding separately

BatchImportFindings accepts 1–100 ASFF records, validates required fields and supported model constraints, reports per-entry failures and replaces records keyed by ProductArn plus Id. Missing Workflow and RecordState default to NEW and ACTIVE

GetFindings string filters: EQUALS/PREFIX/NOT_EQUALS on Id, ProductArn, GeneratorId, AwsAccountId, SeverityLabel, WorkflowStatus, RecordState, ResourceType, ResourceId and ComplianceStatus; inclusive RFC3339 Start/End dates on CreatedAt/UpdatedAt. Fields use AND, positive terms within a field use OR, negative terms exclude all their values. Positive and negative terms cannot mix. Unsupported fields/comparisons fail explicitly

GetFindings supports multiple asc/desc sort criteria on supported scalar filter fields plus Title, CreatedAt and UpdatedAt; dates compare instants, ties preserve storage order. Pagination uses snapshot positions, default/maximum 100; concurrent mutations can change page boundaries. Other record lists use storage key order

BatchUpdateFindings stores Workflow, Severity, Note, Confidence, Criticality, VerificationState, Types, UserDefinedFields and RelatedFindings and updates UpdatedAt. Unknown identifiers are unprocessed
Insights validate the same filters and group by supported string filter fields; computed results count distinct values once per finding and rank counts descending with lexical ties
Custom action targets store names/descriptions without invoking actions. Hub tags integrate with Resource Groups Tagging API and RecordsOnly inventory. Records survive SQLite restart

CloudFormation AWS::SecurityHub::Hub, AWS::SecurityHub::Standard and AWS::SecurityHub::Insight; Terraform aws_securityhub_account, aws_securityhub_standards_subscription, aws_securityhub_action_target and aws_securityhub_insight
gaps: Members, invitations, administrators, organization configuration, automation rules, configuration policies, product integrations/subscriptions and finding aggregation are not implemented
No standard/security controls, control enablement, AWS Config rules, compliance evaluation or service-linked behavior. CloudFormation DisabledStandardsControls is unsupported
EventBridge delivery of imported findings and custom action target invocation are future work

ASFF stores only whitelisted fields; resource details and other unsupported members fail explicitly. DateRange, other filter fields/comparisons, resource sort fields, other insight grouping attributes, Providers and StandardsInput are unsupported
Only hubs support tags within this scope. Catalogue excludes newer standards and does not simulate regional availability or asynchronous readiness

amp.title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus
amp.summary: Store Prometheus workspaces, rule groups namespaces, alert manager definitions and logging configurations as metadata without query or remote-write ingestion.
features: Twenty-one pinned REST JSON operations for workspaces, rule groups namespaces, alert manager definitions, logging configurations and native tags, with AWS SDK v2 coverage
Workspaces with alias and KMS key ARN validation, alias-prefix list filtering, status deterministically ACTIVE on read, and TinyStack-hosted Prometheus endpoint URL
Rule groups namespaces storing YAML data with non-empty and name pattern validation and prefix name filtering
Alert manager definitions storing YAML configuration data with Create, Describe, Put, and Delete operations
Logging configuration validating log group ARN format with Create, Describe, Update, and Delete operations
CloudFormation resources AWS::APS::Workspace and AWS::APS::RuleGroupsNamespace with create, update, retag and delete
TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource on workspace and rule groups namespace ARNs; Resource Groups Tagging API integration
Token pagination (default 100, maximum 1000), account and Region isolation, RecordsOnly=true inventory and Terraform amp endpoint key
gaps: No Prometheus data plane: remote-write ingestion, PromQL queries, and Prometheus rules/alert evaluations are not served; prometheusEndpoint returns a mock endpoint URL
Scrapers, workspace configuration, and resource policies are not implemented
Rule group and alert manager YAML payloads are stored as non-empty blobs; YAML syntax and rules are not evaluated
Workspaces transition immediately to ACTIVE without asynchronous provisioning

apprunner.title: AWS App Runner
apprunner.summary: Store App Runner services, revisioned configurations, connections and VPC connectors as metadata over AWS JSON 1.0.
features: Twenty-eight pinned-model operations: service create/describe/list/update/delete, pause/resume, deployment records and operation history; auto scaling create/describe/list/delete and default selection; connections, VPC connectors, observability configurations and native tags

Lifecycle mutations return OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS snapshots and atomically persist RUNNING, PAUSED or DELETED before returning; the next read sees the terminal state, and every operation record is immediately SUCCEEDED. Pause and deployment require RUNNING; resume requires PAUSED. No background timer or runtime work is scheduled

Every input is checked against the model's required, length, range, pattern and enum constraints and fails InvalidRequestException; a source needs exactly one repository, and CPU and memory must be one of the documented values, checked independently without a runtime sizing matrix

Auto scaling and observability configurations have monotonically increasing revisions and Latest flags for the highest revision of each name; name-only and name/revision partial ARNs resolve the latest active matching revision. Lists default LatestOnly to true; unfiltered configuration lists omit inactive revisions, while name-filtered lists include retained tombstones

An account/Region-local DefaultConfiguration auto scaling revision is materialized lazily with MinSize=1, MaxSize=25 and MaxConcurrency=100. UpdateDefaultAutoScalingConfiguration changes the default; services without an ARN select the latest active revision of its name. Associated and default configurations cannot be deleted
Connections remain PENDING_HANDSHAKE; VPC connectors and observability configurations are ACTIVE records. Deletes retain INACTIVE configuration tombstones; deleted connections are removed

Tags are stored in resource records, with native tag operations, Resource Groups Tagging API support, account/Region isolation, shared token pagination and persistent SQLite restart coverage. Omitted MaxResults returns all matching records
Inventory reports RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false. Resource Groups recognizes the four official CloudFormation types; there is no invented connection type

CloudFormation AWS::AppRunner::Service, AWS::AppRunner::AutoScalingConfiguration, AWS::AppRunner::VpcConnector and AWS::AppRunner::ObservabilityConfiguration providers, with Ref and GetAtt, immutable configuration replacement, service updates and tag updates; native environment-variable and secret Name/Value arrays are translated to SDK maps
gaps: No container runtime, builds, repository clone/authentication, source polling, automatic deployments, traffic, DNS, health checks, metrics, tracing, IAM role use, KMS encryption or network provisioning. Source, instance, encryption, network, observability and health-check settings are records only
ServiceUrl is a deterministic placeholder host derived from the stored service ID and Region; it is not served and has no traffic
No custom domains or VPC ingress connections. ListServicesForAutoScalingConfiguration is not implemented

Deleted service records and inactive configuration revisions are retained indefinitely; no AWS cleanup delay is emulated. Latest refers to the highest stored revision, including retained tombstones, while partial ARNs select active revisions
App Runner referenced network and observability settings are stored without provisioning or cross-service validation; no AWS quotas or external provider handshakes are simulated
CloudFormation service optional-property removal is rejected when the API cannot clear it. Service tag changes are applied in place

amplify.title: AWS Amplify Hosting
amplify.summary: Store Hosting apps, branches, jobs, domain associations, webhooks and backend environment metadata without builds, deployments or DNS.
features: 34 of 37 pinned REST JSON operations, using the official AWS SDK v2, with account and Region isolation and SQLite restart coverage
App and branch CRUD stores build specs, environment variables, redirect rules, auth settings, roles and configuration; defaultDomain is the deterministic placeholder <appId>.amplifyapp.com
Basic auth credentials are stored but omitted from app, branch, nested auto-branch configuration and inventory responses; accessToken and oauthToken are validated then discarded, never returned

StartJob accepts RELEASE and RETRY: jobs remain PENDING until StopJob sets CANCELLED. RETRY allocates a new monotonic branch-local ID and copies source commit metadata; GetJob returns no steps or artifacts
CreateDeployment records a CREATED manual job and optional fileMap with inert amplify.invalid zip or per-file URLs; StartDeployment changes it to PENDING or records a source URL without fetching it
Domain association CRUD always reports PENDING_VERIFICATION, unverified subdomains and no DNS records, including custom certificates; no real DNS or certificate provisioning
Webhook CRUD returns inert amplify.invalid URLs; backend environment Create/Get/List/Delete stores stack and artifact names without creating resources (the model has no UpdateBackendEnvironment)

TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource for apps and branches, Resource Groups Tagging API integration, inventory with RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false, and AWS::Amplify::App/Branch/Domain resource-group types

Every input is checked against the model's required, length, range, pattern and enum constraints and fails BadRequestException; tag sets follow the shared tagging limits and CUSTOM certificates need customCertificateArn
Token pagination with common.Page: apps default/max 100; other collections default/max 50; model maxResults=0 uses the default

GenerateAccessLogs, GetArtifactUrl and ListArtifacts are not implemented
Zip upload URLs, per-file upload URLs and webhook URLs are inert and cannot receive uploads or trigger jobs

CloudFormation domain completion means the record exists, not DNS verification; the underlying domain remains PENDING_VERIFICATION

resourceexplorer2.title: AWS Resource Explorer
resourceexplorer2.summary: Search TinyStack inventory using regional indexes and views.
features: Twenty REST JSON operations for indexes, views, default associations, inventory searches and resource tags; generated model constraint validation.
Create and update finish synchronously as ACTIVE; delete removes the index, its views and default association synchronously and returns DELETED. One index per Region and one AGGREGATOR per account.

Search and ListResources evaluate the query and the view filter as AWS documents: keywords are joined with OR, and that group and every filter with AND; a filter's comma-separated values are alternatives, a trailing * matches any suffix and a leading - excludes matches. Filters: accountid:, id:, region: (global resources report the Region global), resourcetype:service:type, service:, tag:key=value, tag:all, tag:none, tag.key: and tag.value:; tag filters need a view that includes tags. Keywords match the ARN or name case-insensitively as substrings. Quoted phrases, escapes, other prefixes and boolean words fail ValidationException.

Search uses listing.Scoped and ARN order. Count.TotalResources counts all matches before common.Page pagination. Properties contain tags only when the view includes tags. LastReportedAt is the local inventory snapshot time; the inventory has no AWS discovery timestamps.
ListSupportedResourceTypes derives its deterministic type list from the currently populated regional inventory, not a static AWS catalogue.

GetDefaultView returns an empty response when the index has no default view, and ResourceNotFoundException when there is no regional index. Index and view tags live in their records and are visible to inventory, Resource Groups and Resource Groups Tagging API.

CloudFormation AWS::ResourceExplorer2::Index, AWS::ResourceExplorer2::View and AWS::ResourceExplorer2::DefaultViewAssociation; Terraform aws_resourceexplorer2_index and aws_resourceexplorer2_view with resourceexplorer2 endpoint.
gaps: AGGREGATOR is stored and uniqueness is enforced, but searches remain confined to the index Region because listing.Scoped is regional. Global inventory resources are visible only from us-east-1.
Managed views, organization/cross-account scopes, account-level service configuration, setup, streams and newer operations are not implemented. Scope supports only the caller account root ARN.
No asynchronous indexing, replication, service-linked role creation, or 24-hour aggregator promotion cooldown; searches read live inventory. No relevance ranking or AWS-wide supported-type catalogue.
resourceexplorer2.execution: Live regional inventory search; records-only control plane

servicecatalog.title: AWS Service Catalog
servicecatalog.summary: Store portfolios, products, versions, associations and constraints through an AWS JSON 1.1 records-only control plane.
features: Twenty-eight pinned-model operations for portfolios, products, provisioning artifacts, portfolio/product and IAM or IAM_PATTERN principal associations, and constraints; generated validation returns InvalidParametersException

Product types CLOUD_FORMATION_TEMPLATE, MARKETPLACE, TERRAFORM_OPEN_SOURCE, TERRAFORM_CLOUD and EXTERNAL are accepted as records. ProvisioningArtifactParameters must include Info.LoadTemplateFromURL or Info.TemplateURL. URLs are stored verbatim and never fetched or validated as templates; artifact responses expose the URL under Info.TemplateUrl

Products, artifacts and constraints are immediately AVAILABLE, meaning their metadata was saved. Artifacts start Active=true and Guidance=DEFAULT; name, description, Active and Guidance can be updated. The last artifact cannot be deleted. Inactive artifacts are omitted from DescribeProduct

Portfolio deletion fails ResourceInUseException while products, principals or constraints are associated. Associated products cannot be deleted, and product disassociation fails while constraints remain

LAUNCH, NOTIFICATION, RESOURCE_UPDATE, STACKSET and TEMPLATE constraints store JSON objects without enforcing their rules. LAUNCH requires exactly one nonempty RoleArn or LocalRoleName. Duplicate LAUNCH or STACKSET constraints and LAUNCH/STACKSET conflicts on a portfolio/product pair fail explicitly

SearchProductsAsAdmin supports PortfolioId; both product searches support Owner and ProductType exact matches and case-insensitive FullTextSearch over name, description and owner. Values within a key are ORed; keys are ANDed. Other filter keys fail explicitly

Lists and searches use storage key order with PageToken pagination (default page size 20); artifact listing is unpaginated as in the model. ID/name selectors are mutually exclusive and ambiguous names fail explicitly

Create tokens replay successful responses and reject parameter changes; tags live in portfolio/product records and are changed through UpdatePortfolio or UpdateProduct AddTags/RemoveTags. Resource Groups Tagging API and inventory are integrated

CloudFormation Portfolio, CloudFormationProduct, PortfolioProductAssociation, PortfolioPrincipalAssociation and LaunchRoleConstraint providers; product artifact configuration changes replace the product. Terraform portfolio, product and both portfolio association resources and endpoint configuration are covered
AWS SDK v2 integration coverage includes all supported operations, associations, errors, pagination, account/Region isolation, tags, CloudFormation and SQLite restart
gaps: ProvisionProduct, DescribeProvisionedProduct, ScanProvisionedProducts, SearchProvisionedProducts, TerminateProvisionedProduct and DescribeRecord are not whitelisted. No templates are deployed and no provisioned-product or execution records are invented
Tag Options, portfolio sharing/organizations, budgets, service actions, AppRegistry, copy product, source connections and newer operations are not implemented

No IAM principal, role or wildcard matching, ownership authorization, constraint enforcement, launch-path resolution, template inspection, template parameter extraction, or CloudFormation/S3 fetching; HasDefaultPath=false and launch paths are empty

SearchProducts returns locally stored products without principal authorization filtering. Sorting, ProductSource and other unimplemented input members are rejected explicitly. AcceptLanguage accepts only empty/default or en (English); other languages and source-portfolio associations fail explicitly
DisableTemplateValidation and ImportFromPhysicalId are unsupported. Only stored URL sources are supported. No template validation is claimed, regardless of product or artifact type

CloudFormation AcceptLanguage, SourceConnection, SourcePortfolioId and ReplaceProvisioningArtifacts are unsupported; CloudFormation product artifact changes replace rather than reconcile versions. Launch-role parameters and descriptions update in place

globalaccelerator.title: AWS Global Accelerator
globalaccelerator.summary: Store standard accelerators, listeners and regional endpoint groups with local endpoint validation, CloudFormation and Terraform support; no traffic forwarding.
features: Twenty-two pinned AWS JSON 1.1 operations for standard accelerator lifecycle, attributes, listeners, endpoint groups, endpoint membership and accelerator tags; generated InvalidArgumentException model validation

Account-global records use request.GlobalScope with an empty Region. Like IAM and Route 53, requests signed in any Region share the same records. AWS serves its global API only in us-west-2; use us-west-2 for SDK/provider compatibility (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/api/API_UpdateAccelerator.html)
CreateAccelerator and UpdateAccelerator return IN_PROGRESS snapshots and atomically persist DEPLOYED; all later Describe/List calls and restarts see DEPLOYED without timers or health probes

Deterministic allocation uses the lowest free slot 1..254 per account: 192.0.2.<slot> and 198.51.100.<slot>, plus 2001:db8::<2*slot+1 in hex> and 2001:db8::<2*slot+2 in hex> for DUAL_STACK. Addresses are unique among live accelerators in an account, remain stable through disable/type updates/restart and may be reused after deletion. Exhausting the 254-slot local documentation address pool returns LimitExceededException; this is a TinyStack fixture capacity, not an AWS quota

DNS labels are a followed by 16 hex digits derived from SHA-256 of the ARN, ending .awsglobalaccelerator.com; dual-stack adds .dualstack.awsglobalaccelerator.com. The a prefix follows AWS documentation (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/api/API_Accelerator.html)

Accelerators must be disabled and have no listeners before deletion. Listeners must have no endpoint groups before deletion. Port ranges must not overlap within a listener or across listeners of the same accelerator and protocol

One endpoint group per Region per listener; endpoint IDs are checked via exported EC2/ELBv2 methods in the endpoint group Region and account. Supports existing application/network load balancer ARNs, running EC2 instance IDs and Elastic IP allocation IDs; missing references fail explicitly

Endpoint descriptions remain INITIAL (unprobed); HealthReason is absent/null. AWS health states are INITIAL, HEALTHY and UNHEALTHY (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/api/API_EndpointDescription.html). Weight, client IP preservation, port overrides, health configuration and traffic dial are stored; interval must be 10 or 30 seconds
Flow log attributes require an existing local S3 bucket in the same account (any Region); enabling requires bucket and prefix. No log objects are written and S3 delivery policies are not evaluated

Create idempotency tokens persist with their resource and reject reuse with different parameters. List operations page in storage key order. Tags live in accelerator records and integrate with inventory, Resource Groups and Resource Groups Tagging

CloudFormation AWS::GlobalAccelerator::Accelerator, AWS::GlobalAccelerator::Listener and AWS::GlobalAccelerator::EndpointGroup; supported mutable properties update in place, Listener.AcceleratorArn and EndpointGroup.ListenerArn/EndpointGroupRegion replace resources

Terraform globalaccelerator endpoint key and aws_globalaccelerator_accelerator, aws_globalaccelerator_listener and aws_globalaccelerator_endpoint_group lifecycle case using a dedicated local Elastic IP; SDK v2 and SQLite restart coverage
gaps: Records only: static documentation IPs and DNS names do not resolve or forward traffic; no anycast networking, listener sockets, endpoint probing, flow-log delivery or data plane

Custom routing accelerators/listeners/groups, cross-account attachments/endpoints, and BYOIP lifecycle operations are not whitelisted; CreateAccelerator.IpAddresses and endpoint AttachmentArn fail explicitly as unsupported inputs. Terraform provider v5.100.0 unconditionally requests unsupported ListCrossAccountResources for ARN endpoints, even same-account load balancers; the Terraform case uses an Elastic IP endpoint to avoid that unsupported API
Accelerator event history, AWS deployment timing and AWS network-zone topology are not simulated; network zone labels zone-1 and zone-2 are local fixtures
Client IP preservation and endpoint compatibility settings are stored; no packets, routing policies, security-group reachability or load balancer TLS traffic behavior is executed

dsql.title: Amazon Aurora DSQL
dsql.summary: Manage Aurora DSQL cluster records, reciprocal multi-Region peering and versioned cluster policies.
features: Twelve of sixteen pinned REST JSON operations: cluster create/get/list/update/delete, VPC endpoint discovery, policy get/put/delete and three tagging operations; generated ValidationException constraints
Durable transaction-claimed CREATING, ACTIVE, UPDATING, PENDING_SETUP, PENDING_DELETE and DELETING transitions; 100 ms polling with 150 ms minimum transition delay, resumed after SQLite restart
Deletion protection defaults to enabled; successful client-token responses persist independently of resource lifetime, including delete and policy replay
Reciprocal two-cluster peering requires existing clusters in different Regions of the same account, a shared third witness Region and a common documented continent Region set
Public endpoint <identifier>.dsql.<region>.on.aws, cluster ARN, AWS-owned encryption metadata and deterministic cluster-specific PrivateLink service/DNS metadata
Tags in cluster records, storage-key-order pagination, inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API integration

CloudFormation AWS::DSQL::Cluster with in-place updates and no replacement properties, identifier Ref and endpoint attributes; Terraform aws_dsql_cluster and reciprocal aws_dsql_cluster_peering using two regional provider aliases against one endpoint
gaps: Records only, including when the RDS Docker runtime is enabled: no PostgreSQL listener, SQL execution, TLS, IAM database-token authentication, replication, quorum or actual PrivateLink networking. RDS Docker requires fixed database passwords and owns RDS-specific container labels, volumes and lifecycle; safely accepting rotating DSQL IAM tokens needs a PostgreSQL authentication proxy and a separate recovery contract. No RDS code or behavior is changed

IDLE and INACTIVE are not synthesized: AWS describes inactivity triggers without deterministic timing, and this records-only service has no connection activity. Deleted records disappear after DELETING rather than retaining a DELETED tombstone
KmsEncryptionKey accepts only AWS_OWNED_KMS_KEY; custom KMS keys and encryption changes fail ValidationException. EncryptionDetails describes AWS-owned metadata only

Resource policy JSON objects and Statement presence are checked; policies are stored without enforcement. Lockout safety evaluation is unsupported, so create/put with a policy requires bypassPolicyLockoutSafetyCheck=true; CloudFormation PolicyDocument therefore fails explicitly rather than bypassing safety on behalf of the caller
Removing CloudFormation MultiRegionProperties is explicitly unsupported; no implicit replacement. CloudFormation exposes PolicyVersion and AWS-owned EncryptionDetails attributes
The four CDC stream operations are not whitelisted; no change stream delivery, backups, capacity scaling, regional failures, IAM policy enforcement or account quotas
Terraform multi-Region peering requires normal parallel apply: both reciprocal aws_dsql_cluster_peering resources must run concurrently. Serial apply can wait indefinitely for the reciprocal request

Client token replay records have no expiry. Region sets follow the documented AWS availability snapshot; cluster-specific PrivateLink suffixes are locally derived and do not correspond to AWS infrastructure
dsql.execution: Records only; deterministic background control-plane transitions

fis.title: AWS Fault Injection Service
fis.summary: Store experiment templates and execute aws:fis:wait actions locally with durable wall-clock state, dependencies, and alarm stop conditions.
features: Sixteen pinned REST JSON operations for experiment templates, experiments, executable action discovery, target-type discovery and tags; model constraint validation returns ValidationException
Create, get, list, update and delete templates with action dependency and cycle validation; only aws:fis:wait is accepted
ISO 8601 wait durations from one minute to 12 hours, matching the AWS action reference; independent actions run concurrently and startAfter dependencies wait for completion
Start, get, list and stop experiments with transaction-claimed pending, initiating, running, completed, stopping, stopped and failed transitions; per-action status and timestamps
StopExperiment stops initiating/running actions and cancels pending actions; CloudWatch metric and composite alarm stop conditions stop execution in ALARM state
IAM role ARN, CloudWatch alarm ARN, CloudWatch Logs group and S3 log-destination existence checks through local service APIs
Targets preserve resourceArns, resourceTags, filters and parameters; selectionMode ALL, COUNT(n) and PERCENT(n) is validated; wait actions accept no targets
Persistent experiment snapshots and partition-wide worker index resume elapsed wall-clock waits after SQLite restart; templates may be edited or deleted without altering running snapshots
Template and experiment tags, Resource Groups Tagging API and inventory integration; storage-key-order list pagination and template-filtered experiments
CloudFormation AWS::FIS::ExperimentTemplate supports in-place updates; Terraform aws_fis_experiment_template and fis endpoint override
gaps: The full AWS action catalog is unsupported: EC2, EBS, ECS, EKS, RDS, network, SSM, CloudWatch, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Kinesis, Lambda, S3, ARC and every action other than aws:fis:wait. Unsupported action IDs fail validation by name; no infrastructure fault effects are simulated
ListTargetResourceTypes returns an empty list and GetTargetResourceType returns ResourceNotFoundException because wait has no targets. Stored template targets are not resolved, sampled or modified
Experiment target account configurations, multi-account experiments, experiment options, safety levers, experiment reports and ListExperimentResolvedTargets are not whitelisted
Log configuration is stored and destination existence is validated; no experiment logs are emitted to CloudWatch Logs or S3
Worker steps are polled every 100 milliseconds; downtime counts toward an already-running wait. Alarm lookups occur before each transactional step, so changes are observed on the next poll
Role existence is validated, but role assumption, IAM trust-policy evaluation and remote AWS calls are not performed. Client-token replay is scoped to retained resource records
fis.execution: Real local wait actions; all other fault actions unsupported

shield.title: AWS Shield Advanced
shield.summary: Store Shield Advanced subscriptions, protections and protection groups without attack detection or mitigation.
features: Thirty-three JSON 1.1 operations with generated InvalidParameterException validation and AWS SDK v2 integration coverage
Annual subscription commitment, renewal-window validation and global account-scoped persistence
Protections validate existing CloudFront distributions, Route 53 hosted zones, Global Accelerator accelerators, Classic/Application Load Balancers and Elastic IP allocations
Protection groups support ALL, BY_RESOURCE_TYPE and ARBITRARY membership, filters and pagination
Route 53 health checks, emergency contacts, proactive engagement and SRT role/log bucket configuration with local reference checks
Tags, Resource Groups Tagging API and records-only inventory for protections and protection groups
CloudFormation Protection, ProtectionGroup, DRTAccess and ProactiveEngagement; Terraform subscription, protection and protection group
gaps: No attack detection, traffic inspection, mitigation, SRT calls, IAM policy evaluation, support-plan checks or DDoS cost protection; attack lists and statistics are empty and unknown attacks fail
Application layer automatic response operations and WAFv2 integration are unsupported
Network Load Balancers are protected through their Elastic IP allocations, as on AWS; direct NLB ARNs are unsupported
Subscriptions cannot be deleted; DeleteSubscription returns LockedSubscriptionException. No billing or automatic renewal scheduler runs

iotwireless.title: AWS IoT Wireless
iotwireless.summary: Store LoRaWAN resources and simulate local uplinks through the IoT MQTT broker and topic rules.
features: 68 REST JSON operations with generated ValidationException constraints; destinations, LoRaWAN and Sidewalk device profiles, service profiles, LoRaWAN devices and gateways, multicast groups and FUOTA tasks

Destinations validate existing TinyStack IAM roles and IoT topic rules or publishable MQTT topics; devices validate destinations and profile references, activation mode and unique DevEui; gateways enforce unique GatewayEui
Things and gateway certificates associate with real TinyStack IoT resources; lookup devices and gateways by ID, EUI or associated thing name

TestWirelessDevice commits a simulated uplink before publishing through IoT Core: MQTT destinations deliver to subscribers and RuleName destinations invoke that rule using Basic Ingest, including SQS actions

Uplinks contain WirelessDeviceId, base64 PayloadData (Test), and WirelessMetadata.LoRaWAN. FPort is the first configured application port or 1; data rate 3, frequency 868300000 Hz, RSSI -64 and SNR 9.5 are deterministic. All gateways in the account and Region participate; last-uplink timestamps and gateway Connected status derive only from this traffic
Device and multicast downlinks queue durably without transmission; list device queues with pagination and delete a MessageId or * for all messages

Multicast device and FUOTA device/group associations; multicast sessions become Session_Set at their start time and return to Pending after SessionTimeout seconds or cancellation. FUOTA tasks progress FuotaSession_Waiting to In_FuotaSession to FuotaDone, with a 0.6-second session and Successful associated device status

A services/background.Group worker visits a durable aws/iotwireless/index every 200 milliseconds, claims transitions in transactions and resumes after SQLite restart; FUOTA firmware references must name existing TinyStack S3 objects and IAM roles
Stored service and per-resource log levels; GetServiceEndpoint returns this TinyStack endpoint for CUPS and its ws/wss equivalent for LNS
Tags on all seven resource kinds, inventory, Resource Groups and Resource Groups Tagging API; list pagination in storage key order and idempotent create tokens

CloudFormation Destination, DeviceProfile, ServiceProfile, MulticastGroup and FuotaTask, with immutable destination name and profile name/LoRaWAN replacement; mutable fields and tags update in place. FUOTA LoRaWAN.StartTime starts the task after associations
Terraform AWS provider 5.100.0 has no iotwireless resources or service endpoint key (verified complete upstream source tree); no Terraform resources, endpoint override or update-apply count changes
gaps: No radio transmission, LoRaWAN network server, CUPS/LNS listener or server trust certificate, firmware transfer, real gateway health, positioning or IAM role assumption/policy evaluation; local statistics are simulation values only

Sidewalk wireless devices and manufacturing-serial lookup require unsupported partner account linking; Sidewalk device profiles are records with a locally generated public-key identifier and false qualification status
Partner accounts, network analyzer, positioning/GetPositionEstimate, import tasks, gateway task definitions/tasks/firmware, event configurations and metrics are not whitelisted

CloudFormation WirelessDevice and WirelessGateway are unsupported: their mutable full radio/activation/EUI properties cannot be completely expressed through the implemented update APIs. Sidewalk CloudFormation profiles and service-profile derived radio attributes absent from the API are unsupported

FUOTA tasks and their associations can change only before starting; started tasks cannot be restarted. Multicast group queues have no list API and remain until group deletion. Log levels are stored without log emission
iotwireless.execution: Local simulated uplinks through IoT MQTT and rules; durable downlink records and deterministic multicast/FUOTA worker; no radio transport

mediaconnect.title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect
mediaconnect.summary: Store flows, sources, outputs, entitlements and VPC interfaces with durable local lifecycle transitions; no media is transported.
features: Twenty-two REST JSON operations with model constraints reported as BadRequestException

Create, describe, list, update and delete flows; StartFlow and StopFlow use STANDBY, STARTING, ACTIVE, STOPPING, UPDATING and DELETING states. A durable partition-wide index is claimed transactionally every 100 milliseconds, with one deterministic transition per visit and recovery after SQLite restart
Sources with RTP, RTP-FEC, RIST, Zixi push and SRT listener/caller records, up to two sources with failover configuration; SRT merge is rejected
Outputs with RTP, RTP-FEC, RIST, Zixi push/pull and SRT listener/caller records, update and removal; up to 50 outputs per flow
Grant, update, revoke and page entitlements; cross-account sources resolve enabled entitlements in the same Region and require the receiving account to be a subscriber

VPC interface records validate existing TinyStack EC2 subnets/security groups in the same VPC and Availability Zone, and existing account IAM roles; Zixi static-key and SRT password encryption validate existing Secrets Manager secrets in the same account and Region
Tags on flow, source, output and entitlement records (CreateFlow FlowTags or TagResource), inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API integration; list pagination follows storage key order
CloudFormation AWS::MediaConnect::Flow, FlowSource, FlowOutput, FlowEntitlement and FlowVpcInterface with specification-driven replacement and complete in-place template updates

Terraform provider 5.100 has no MediaConnect resources (verified internal/service/mediaconnect at v5.100.0); endpoint key and local Terraform CLI override are supplied; no resource/update-apply count changes
gaps: Records only: no media transport, sockets, ingest/egress IPs, EC2 network-interface allocation, health monitoring, actual failover or encryption/key retrieval; lifecycle ACTIVE does not indicate media delivery

Media streams, source metadata/thumbnails, maintenance, monitoring configuration, flow sizing, NDI, CDI, JPEG XS, router integration, bridges, gateways, offerings and reservations are unsupported and not whitelisted
VPC interface tags are unsupported, including the CloudFormation Tags property
SPEKE configuration is stored for entitlement encryption without contacting the key server; IAM trust and permission policies are not evaluated
Cross-account entitlement changes do not asynchronously modify existing receiver flow status; references are rechecked on source changes and StartFlow
mediaconnect.execution: Records only; deterministic local flow lifecycle worker

accessanalyzer.title: IAM Access Analyzer
accessanalyzer.summary: Store analyzers and archive rules as records with deterministic validation, empty findings, and CloudFormation/Terraform support.
features: Nineteen pinned REST JSON operations for analyzers, archive rules, findings, and resource tags, with AWS SDK v2 coverage
Every input is checked against the model's required, length, pattern and enum constraints and fails ValidationException
Analyzers with account and organization types, unused access configuration validation (1..365 days), and status immediately ACTIVE on read
Archive rules with filter criteria validation (eq, neq, contains, exists), list pagination, and inline creation during analyzer setup (inline rule names must be unique)
CloudFormation resource AWS::AccessAnalyzer::Analyzer with inline archive rules, configuration updates, and resource deletion
TagResource, UntagResource, ListTagsForResource on analyzer ARNs; Resource Groups Tagging API integration
Deterministic gaps: analyzers produce no findings; ListFindings and ListFindingsV2 return empty results; GetFinding, GetFindingV2, and UpdateFindings return ResourceNotFoundException
Records-only inventory and Terraform accessanalyzer endpoint key

No organization validation: ORGANIZATION analyzers are accepted as records without querying AWS Organizations
ValidatePolicy, CheckNoNewAccess, CheckAccessNotGranted, CheckNoPublicAccess, access previews, and policy generation are not supported
StartResourceScan, analyzed resources, and recommendations are not supported

networkfirewall.title: AWS Network Firewall
networkfirewall.summary: Store Network Firewall rule groups, policies, firewalls, and logging configurations without packet inspection or endpoint network provisioning.
features: Records-only control plane using the official AWS SDK v2, with account and Region isolation and SQLite restart coverage
Stateless and stateful rule group CRUD, capacity validation, metadata description, and rule source parsing
Firewall policy CRUD with stateless default actions, rule group associations, and stateful engine options
Every input is checked against the model's required, length, pattern and enum constraints and fails InvalidRequestException
Firewall lifecycle with subnets read from TinyStack EC2 (each in the firewall's VPC and a distinct Availability Zone), deterministic endpoint IDs and sync states; DeleteFirewall reports DELETING
Delete protection, policy change protection, and subnet change protection guards
Logging configuration management for Alert and Flow logs targeting CloudWatch, S3, or Kinesis Firehose destinations
Resource policies (Put, Describe, Delete) are stored on firewall policies and rule groups; they grant no cross-account access
Standard TagResource, UntagResource, and ListTagsForResource APIs with Resource Groups Tagging API integration
CloudFormation AWS::NetworkFirewall::Firewall, AWS::NetworkFirewall::FirewallPolicy, AWS::NetworkFirewall::RuleGroup, and AWS::NetworkFirewall::LoggingConfiguration resources
Terraform aws_networkfirewall_rule_group, aws_networkfirewall_firewall_policy, and aws_networkfirewall_firewall integration
gaps: Records only: no packet inspection, Suricata engine execution, traffic filtering, VPC route table updates, or actual ENI network data plane endpoints
VPC endpoints and sync states are deterministic mock records reporting READY status
TLS inspection configurations and rule group analysis/summary metrics are outside the subset
Transit gateway attached firewalls are not supported: CreateFirewall requires VpcId and SubnetMappings

inspector2.title: Amazon Inspector
inspector2.summary: Records-only scanning state, configuration and findings filters. No scanning is performed; findings and coverage remain empty.
features: Eighteen of 81 pinned REST JSON operations, with generated model constraint validation returning ValidationException
Enable, Disable and BatchGetAccountStatus for EC2, ECR, LAMBDA, LAMBDA_CODE and CODE_REPOSITORY, restricted to the caller account; foreign accountIds fail explicitly

ENABLING becomes ENABLED and DISABLING becomes DISABLED inside the same transaction; Enable and Disable return the final state immediately. Overall account status is ENABLED while any scan type is enabled; Disable without resourceTypes disables all types; Enable clientToken responses are persisted indefinitely, with conflicting resourceTypes rejected

GetConfiguration and UpdateConfiguration record ECR rescan duration and EC2 scan mode. Defaults are DAYS_14 and EC2_HYBRID, matching https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-resources.html; updates become SUCCESS immediately, with no scanner side effects

CreateFilter, ListFilters, UpdateFilter and DeleteFilter store NONE/SUPPRESS filters, names, descriptions, reasons and supported FilterCriteria. Model constraints and range ordering are validated; lists paginate in storage key order

TagResource, UntagResource and ListTagsForResource for filters, resource inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API integration
CloudFormation AWS::InspectorV2::Filter and Terraform aws_inspector2_enabler / aws_inspector2_filter with the inspector2 endpoint key
SQLite restart preserves scan settings, configuration, filters and tags
gaps: No scanners, vulnerability evaluation, findings generation, suppression execution or resource discovery: enabling scans never produces findings or coverage. No finding or coverage records are invented
No delegated administrator, members, organization configuration or configuration inheritance; only the caller account is supported

No CIS scans or AWS::InspectorV2::CisScanConfiguration, SBOM or findings exports, vulnerability search, encryption keys, code security operations, connectors, deep inspection or newer multi-cloud behavior

Code-security and multi-cloud FilterCriteria / CoverageFilterCriteria members and aggregation request members are not whitelisted and fail NotImplemented. Only the existing AWS account, AMI, ECR container, EC2 instance, finding type, image layer, package, repository, title, Lambda layer and Lambda function aggregation types are supported
ListAccountPermissions is not implemented: TinyStack does not invent effective Inspector permissions
Only ECR rescanDuration and EC2 scanMode configuration members are supported; pull-date rescan settings and VM scanner activation fail explicitly
CloudFormation updates a filter's Description in place and replaces the filter only when Description is removed, since UpdateFilter cannot clear it

swf.title: Amazon Simple Workflow Service
swf.summary: Coordinate local deciders and activity workers through durable workflow histories, task polling, timers and timeouts.
features: All 39 pinned JSON 1.0 operations: domains, workflow/activity types, executions, decision and activity tasks, visibility counts and tags; generated model constraints return ValidationException

Domain registration, deprecation and restoration; workflow/activity type versions, defaults, deprecation, restoration and deletion; retention accepts 0..90 days or NONE (0 and NONE remove closed history)

Start, describe, signal, cancel, terminate and continue executions; one open run per workflowId per domain; execution tags, ordered histories, reverse-order pagination and visibility time/type/tag/workflowId/close-status filters with the one-filter rule

Real local deciders and activity workers: 60-second cancellable long polls wake on in-process changes, claim tasks in storage transactions, respect priorities and invalidate opaque tokens when tasks close

management requests; the engine handles indexing and search. Do not claim AWS
security or cluster topology features from an unconfigured single container.

another. Runtime launch and health checks happen outside storage transactions.

the returned endpoint, restart, and delete. Verify index isolation, unsupported
configuration errors, failed launch cleanup, memory/port limits, tags, and
management response parity against AWS captures.
